records.title: Stop the screensaver and lock firing over a fullscreen Steam game
records.symptom:
A fullscreen Steam or Proton game played with a controller gets the Omarchy screensaver drawn over it after the idle timeout, and the lock screen follows. Mouse and keyboard activity prevent it, controller input does not. `hyprctl clients -j` shows the game with `inhibitingIdle: false`:

```json
{
  "class": "steam_app_244210",
  "title": "Assetto Corsa",
  "fullscreen": 2,
  "xwayland": true,
  "inhibitingIdle": false
}
```

Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 with Hyprland 0.56.2, by four users with different controllers (DualSense, GameSir Cyclone 2, Steam Controller).
records.cause: Omarchy's default Steam rule in `default/hypr/apps/steam.lua` is `o.window("steam", { float = true, idle_inhibit = "fullscreen" })`. `o.window` with a string sets `match.class` to that string, and Hyprland class matches are full-regex matches, so the rule applies to the Steam client (class `steam`) and not to games, whose XWayland class is `steam_app_<appid>`. Games run through gamescope expose the class `gamescope` instead and miss the rule the same way. Still the shipped default on `quattro` and on omarchy 4.0.2-1. The controller does not reset the compositor idle timer on its own, so with no inhibitor the idle timeout runs during play.
records.fix:
Add rules for the game window classes to the end of `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, below the `Add any other personal Hyprland configuration below` comment:

```lua
-- ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua
o.window("steam_app_.*", { idle_inhibit = "fullscreen" })
o.window("gamescope", { idle_inhibit = "fullscreen" })
```

Reload and check the config parsed:

```bash
hyprctl reload
hyprctl configerrors
```

`steam_app_.*` covers Proton games. A native Linux game can use its own class, so if one still triggers the screensaver, read its class while it is running and add a rule for it:

```bash
hyprctl clients -j | jq '.[] | {class, initialClass, title, fullscreen, inhibitingIdle}'
```

One reporter used `idle_inhibit = "focus"` instead for games run borderless-windowed rather than fullscreen. Nobody else confirmed that variant.
records.verify:
With the game fullscreen, the window now reports the inhibitor, and normal idle locking resumes when the game is closed:

```bash
hyprctl clients -j | jq '.[] | select(.class | test("^steam_app_|^gamescope")) | {class, fullscreen, inhibitingIdle}'
```

Expected `"fullscreen": 2` and `"inhibitingIdle": true`. Two reporters confirmed controller-only play past the idle timeout with neither screensaver nor lock activating.

records.title: Fix `Invalid TOML in config file: ~/.config/mise/config.toml` that keeps coming back
records.symptom:
Every mise-backed tool (`gh`, `claude`, `codex`, `opencode` and the rest of the wrappers in `~/.local/bin`) fails with:

```
mise::config::parse_error
Invalid TOML in config file: ~/.config/mise/config.toml
key with no value, expected `=`
```

The file ends in a fragment of a previous entry:

```toml
[tools]
gh = "latest"
st"
```

Deleting and recreating the file does not help, the fragment returns. The quieter form of the same bug is entries silently vanishing from `[tools]`, so a tool that worked yesterday now says it is not installed, and mise shims for services break with `mise ERROR No version is set for shim: npm`. Reported on Omarchy 4.0 with mise 2026.8.3 and again on 4.0.0.alpha after the 2026-08-19 upgrade.
records.cause:
Two mise bugs, both established by the maintainers' triage and by the reporter, who wrote the upstream fix. Every wrapper `omarchy-mise-install` writes into `~/.local/bin` runs `mise use -g <tool>` on every launch, which rewrites the whole global `config.toml`. Before mise 2026.8.7 that rewrite was in place rather than write-then-rename, so a shorter config written over a longer one left the tail of the old file behind: `[tools]
claude = "latest"
` is 26 bytes, `[tools]
gh = "latest"
` is 22, and bytes 22 to 25 of the first are `st"`. Underneath that, `mise use -g` read and wrote the file with no lock, so two wrappers starting together lost each other's entries. Anything that launches a wrapper at high frequency makes it worse: an IDE polling GitHub through the `gh` wrapper produced 2,438 writes in two minutes and emptied a five-tool config within seconds.
records.fix:
Both fixes are in mise 2026.8.7 (released 2026-08-17): `#12040` writes the config atomically and `#12069` preserves concurrent global config updates. Omarchy ships mise as the `mise-bin` package, so update and confirm the version:

```bash
omarchy update
mise --version        # 2026.8.7 or later
```

Then repair the file. If it is invalid TOML, move it aside, list the packages your wrappers expect, and re-add them in one command:

```bash
mv ~/.config/mise/config.toml ~/.config/mise/config.toml.bad
grep -h 'mise use -g' ~/.local/bin/*      # one line per wrapper, naming its package
mise use -g gh claude codex               # the packages from that list
```

If the file is valid but entries went missing, skip the `mv` and run only the `mise use -g` line with the missing packages.

Until the update has landed, launch wrapped tools one at a time rather than several at once. Two wrapper-side mitigations were posted in the thread (an `flock` around `mise use -g`, and skipping the write when `mise ls --current <tool>` already lists it) but each was confirmed by one person only, and `omarchy update` regenerates the wrappers over any edit.
records.verify:
```bash
mise --version
cat ~/.config/mise/config.toml   # valid TOML, every wrapped tool listed under [tools]
gh --version
```

The two mise pull requests are the confirmation: the atomic write removes the `st"` fragment and the concurrent-update fix stops entries being lost. Nobody in the thread has yet posted a post-2026.8.7 result, and the issue is still open.

records.title: Apply a shell plugin edit that the automatic reload silently ignores
records.symptom: You edit a plugin under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<id>/` (or run `omarchy plugin update <id>`). The shell logs `Local plugin changed, reloading: <id>` and re-creates the widget or service, but it keeps running the old code: a changed label never appears, a `Component.onCompleted: console.warn(...)` marker never fires, and a service's `IpcHandler` still answers with the previous behaviour. Reported by four plugin authors on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 with quickshell 0.3.0 (r20.g28771c7) and Qt 6.11.2, for bar widgets and for service plugins.
records.cause: Confirmed in source by the maintainers' triage against `quattro`. The reload path in `shell/shell.qml` guards its cache flush with `if (typeof Qt.clearComponentCache === "function") Qt.clearComponentCache()`, but `clearComponentCache()` is a plain C++ method on `QQmlEngine` and is not exposed on the QML `Qt` object, so the branch never runs. Every plugin entry point is loaded by a URL that does not change when a file is edited, so the engine hands back the previously compiled component. The guard has been dead since it arrived in 4.0.0-beta3 and is still there on `quattro` and in omarchy 4.0.2-1 (`shell.qml` line 757 in `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/`). Two pull requests offer fixes, `#9606` (restart the shell when the cache cannot be cleared, closed unmerged on 2026-09-06) and `#8766` (`Quickshell.reload(false)`, open and blocked on an upstream quickshell teardown bug).
records.fix:
Restart the shell after any plugin change. A fresh process compiles the plugin from source:

```bash
omarchy restart shell      # same as: omarchy-restart-shell
```

Do not use `omarchy refresh shell` for this. That command runs `omarchy-refresh-config omarchy/shell.json` and `omarchy-bar defaults` before restarting, so it resets your shell configuration. `omarchy-restart-shell` refuses to run while the session is locked, so unlock first.
records.verify:
Add a marker to the plugin before restarting and look for it afterwards:

```qml
Component.onCompleted: console.warn("plugin reloaded")
```

```bash
omarchy restart shell
journalctl --user -b -t omarchy-shell -n 50 --no-pager | grep 'plugin reloaded'
```

Three reporters confirmed the marker fires only after the restart, never after the automatic reload.

records.title: Finish an Omarchy 4.0 install that stops at `Module psmouse not found`
records.symptom:
A clean Omarchy 4.0.0 (Quattro) install halts during the `Configuring system` phase with:

```
modprobe: FATAL: Module psmouse not found in directory /lib/modules/7.1.8-arch1-Watanare-T2-2-t2
[Failed]: /usr/share/omarchy/install/hardware/fix-synaptic-touchpad.sh (exit code: 1)
```

It does not matter whether you picked full-disk or free-space install. Reported on a ThinkPad, an IdeaPad L340 and an IdeaPad 330-15IKB, and by two further users on full-disk installs. If you patch around it and resume by hand, the next hardware scripts fail with `error: failed retrieving file '...' from disk : Could not open file /var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline/...` even with working internet.
records.cause: Established by the maintainers' triage and fixed in `#7236`. `install/hardware/fix-synaptic-touchpad.sh` fires on any machine with an input device merely named `synaptics` and runs `modprobe psmouse synaptics_intertouch=1`. During an install it runs inside `arch-chroot`, where `uname -r` still names the live ISO's `linux-t2` kernel while `/lib/modules` holds the target's stock `linux`, so modprobe cannot find the module, and because the hardware phase runs under `set -euo pipefail` the whole install stops. The follow-on `Could not open file /var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline/...` errors are a consequence of resuming by hand: the installer bind-mounts the ISO's offline mirror into the target and unmounts it when it exits, leaving an empty directory that the target's `pacman.conf` still names as its only repository. That part is the triage's reading of the source, not something a reporter measured.
records.fix:
Install from the v4.0.1 ISO or later. `#7236` was merged into `quattro` on 2026-08-24 and the v4.0.1 release (2026-08-25) carries the corrected script, which asks `modprobe -qn psmouse` first and warns instead of failing. Two reporters confirmed the fix is in that ISO. Installing Omarchy 3.6 and upgrading also avoids it, because the script only runs from the ISO.

If you are stuck mid-install with the 4.0.0 ISO, patch the script in the target from the live environment. Two reporters confirmed this gets past the touchpad step:

```bash
sed -i 's|^\(\s*modprobe psmouse synaptics_intertouch=1\).*|\1 2>/dev/null \|\| true|' \
  /mnt/usr/share/omarchy/install/hardware/fix-synaptic-touchpad.sh
grep -n modprobe /mnt/usr/share/omarchy/install/hardware/fix-synaptic-touchpad.sh
```

Before resuming, put the offline mirror back so the remaining hardware scripts can find their packages. This step is the triage's proposed resume and was not confirmed by a reporter, but the reporters who skipped it hit the `Could not open file` errors on every following script:

```bash
mount --bind /var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline /mnt/var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline
findmnt /mnt/var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline
ls /mnt/var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline | head
```

Then resume the way the original reporter did, with your install username:

```bash
arch-chroot /mnt /usr/bin/omarchy-apply-system --install-user <user> --first-install
```
records.verify:
On a v4.0.1 or later ISO the corrected script is in place:

```bash
grep -n 'modprobe -qn psmouse' /usr/share/omarchy/install/hardware/fix-synaptic-touchpad.sh
```

After a resumed 4.0.0 install, the `[Failed]` line does not recur and the hardware scripts complete. One reporter confirmed the rest of the install finished after patching the touchpad script and restoring package access.
records.danger: Resuming a half-finished install by hand skips whatever the installer had not yet reached. If anything after the hardware phase also fails, reinstall from the v4.0.1 ISO rather than patching further, or the target may not boot cleanly.

records.title: Recover a link saturated by orphaned `omarchy-network-speedtest` workers
records.symptom: After running the shell's Speed Test panel and closing it before it finished (clicking away, or the shell restarting during the test), the internet stays very slow for tens of minutes. `ps` shows several `/bin/bash /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-network-speedtest down` (or `up`) processes reparented to `systemd --user`, each with a `curl` pulling from or posting to `*.nflxvideo.net/speedtest`. Reporters measured 300 to 440 Mbit/s of sustained traffic for 31 to 47 minutes, and one upload run reached about 126 GB transmitted before it was killed. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 and 4.0.1-1 with quickshell 0.3.0 and 0.3.1.
records.cause: Established by several reporters reading `bin/omarchy-network-speedtest` and the panel code. The script forks eight `traffic_worker` loops that run `while true` with no duration cap and no `curl --max-time`, and relies on `trap cleanup EXIT` in the parent to reap them. Hiding the panel sends SIGTERM through `Process.running = false` and then destroys the panel `Process` object in the same event-loop turn, so `QProcess` finishes the parent with SIGKILL before its trap has run and the workers are adopted by `systemd --user`. A plain SIGTERM to the parent from a terminal cleans up correctly every time, which is what isolates the leak to the panel teardown. The script is unchanged on `quattro` since 2026-07-22 and `#7598` (bound each worker) and `#9344` (keep the panel loaded during cleanup) are both open.
records.fix:
Kill the leftover workers. Three reporters confirmed this restores normal throughput immediately:

```bash
pkill -f omarchy-network-speedtest
pkill -f 'nflxvideo.net/speedtest'     # ends the in-flight curl transfers straight away
```

Until `#7598` or `#9344` lands, let a test run through to the `Run again` button before closing the panel, and do not restart the shell while one is running.
records.verify:
```bash
ps -e -o pid=,ppid=,cmd= | grep -F '/omarchy-network-speedtest' | grep -v grep
pgrep -af nflxvideo
```

Both should print nothing. To reproduce the leak deliberately on an unpatched shell, two reporters used:

```bash
omarchy-shell shell summon omarchy.speedtest '{}'
sleep 7
omarchy-shell shell hide omarchy.speedtest
sleep 4
ps -e -o pid=,ppid=,cmd= | grep -F '/omarchy-network-speedtest' | grep -v grep
```

records.title: Unstick migration 1786643346 when it insists a browser window is open
records.symptom: On Omarchy 4.0.0-1 stable, `omarchy update` stops at migration `1786643346` ("Repair the Copy URL shortcut for profiles that predate its pinned extension id"). It says a browser window is open and asks you to close it, even after every browser is closed, after `pkill -f` on all of them, and after several reboots. Confirming the prompt re-prompts forever. Declining exits 1, and because `omarchy-migrate` runs under `set -euo pipefail` and `omarchy-update` calls it under `set -e`, every migration that sorts after it never runs and the rest of the update (post-update hook, AUR packages, mise, orphan cleanup) is skipped.
records.cause:
Established in the thread and confirmed against `migrations/1786643346.sh` on `quattro`: the migration never looks at processes or windows. `profile_open()` decides a Chromium-family profile is open purely from filesystem markers in the profile's user-data-dir:

```bash
[[ -L $1/SingletonLock || -e $1/SingletonLock || -S $1/SingletonSocket ]]
```

Chromium-family browsers create `SingletonLock` as a symlink to `<hostname>-<pid>` and unlink it on a clean exit, but leave it behind after a crash, a `SIGKILL`, or a hard power-off. It lives under `~/.config/`, so a reboot never clears it and `pkill` has nothing left to signal. The guard is a `while` loop, so a marker that is permanently present re-prompts forever. The migration only checks profiles that actually need the repair, so the stale marker can sit in a profile you stopped using long ago (the second reporter's was an old Brave profile).
records.fix:
With every Chromium-family browser genuinely closed, find the stale markers:

```bash
ls -l ~/.config/{chromium,google-chrome*,BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser*,microsoft-edge*,vivaldi,opera,helium}/Singleton* 2>/dev/null
```

Delete the `SingletonLock` (and `SingletonSocket`, if one is there) in whichever profile roots turn up. A dangling symlink to a `<hostname>-<pid>` that no longer exists is the signature. For example:

```bash
rm ~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/SingletonLock
rm -f ~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/SingletonSocket
```

Then run the migrations again, which also finishes the rest of the interrupted update:

```bash
omarchy-migrate
omarchy update
```

PR #7026 makes `profile_open()` check that the PID named by the `SingletonLock` symlink is alive (`kill -0`) and ignore an orphaned lock. It is still open and unmerged as of 2026-09-07, so the manual removal is the fix on every shipped release up to 4.0.2.
records.verify:
```bash
omarchy-migrate                                   # runs to the end without the prompt
ls ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/ | grep 1786643346   # marker written once it completed
```

The marker directory is `STATE_DIR` in `omarchy-migrate` (line 32 on 4.0.2-1). The second reporter confirmed the `ls` command found the stale marker and removing the profile directory let the migration run.
records.danger: Only remove `SingletonLock` while no Chromium-family browser is running. Removing it under a live browser lets a second instance open the same profile, which can corrupt that profile.

records.title: Boot the Omarchy install USB with nomodeset when an NVIDIA machine goes to a black screen
records.symptom: Booting the Omarchy 4 (Quattro) install medium on a machine with an NVIDIA card shows a black screen and never reaches the installer. Reported on an RTX 5060 Ti, an RTX 5060 and an RTX 4090 in this thread, and on an RTX 3060 in #7061. One reporter saw the screen stay black for about 20 seconds, the keyboard backlight go out, and the monitor start its sleep countdown. On UEFI no boot menu is shown at all, so there is nowhere obvious to type a kernel parameter.
records.cause: The workaround is confirmed by three reporters on three cards. The mechanism is the collaborator's reading of the `omarchy-iso` sources, not a reproduction, since nobody triaging had an NVIDIA card: the live ISO's initramfs puts `kms` in HOOKS with no `autodetect`, so every in-tree DRM driver modesets during the live boot, the live medium ships no proprietary NVIDIA driver, so nouveau is the driver in play, and the default entry carries `quiet splash`, so when that takeover fails nothing is left on screen. Exactly what nouveau gets wrong on these cards is not established. The missing UEFI menu is configuration, not a symptom: `configs/grub/grub.cfg` in `omacom-io/omarchy-iso` sets `timeout=0` and `timeout_style=hidden` (confirmed on `quattro` on 2026-09-07), so GRUB boots the default entry on every UEFI machine without drawing anything. Legacy BIOS boots show a syslinux menu for 15 seconds (`TIMEOUT 150`). `nomodeset` is needed on the live medium only. The installed system boots normally without it afterwards, confirmed on the 4090.
records.fix:
Add `nomodeset` to the live medium's kernel command line for that one boot.

**Legacy BIOS boot.** The syslinux menu is visible for 15 seconds. Highlight `Omarchy install medium (x86_64, BIOS)`, press Tab, append ` nomodeset` to the end of the line, press Enter.

**UEFI boot, if you can raise the hidden GRUB menu.** Hold Shift from the moment the firmware hands off. This is a GRUB side effect that depends on the firmware reporting modifier state, so it may do nothing. If a menu appears, highlight `Omarchy`, press `e`, find the line beginning `linux`, append ` nomodeset`, and press Ctrl-X.

**UEFI boot, no menu at all.** Get to the `grub>` prompt (one reporter reached it with Shift+Esc during boot, on one machine) and boot the live kernel by hand. The paths and arguments are the shipped default entry with `archisosearchuuid=` swapped for `archisosearchfilename=`, because the UUID is not known at a bare prompt:

```
search --file --set=root /arch/boot/x86_64/vmlinuz-linux-t2
linux /arch/boot/x86_64/vmlinuz-linux-t2 archisobasedir=arch archisosearchfilename=/arch/boot/x86_64/vmlinuz-linux-t2 quiet splash xe.enable_panel_replay=0 initramfs_async=0 nomodeset
initrd /arch/boot/x86_64/initramfs-linux-t2.img
boot
```

If the screen still goes black, drop `quiet splash` from that `linux` line so the last kernel message stays visible.

The installer then runs as normal, and the installed system does not need `nomodeset`. A proper fix, an `Omarchy with safe graphics` menu entry with a visible three second menu, is `omacom-io/omarchy-iso#110`. It is open and unmerged as of 2026-09-07, so the 4.0.0, 4.0.1 and 4.0.2 ISOs all carry the hidden menu and no safe entry.
records.verify: The Omarchy logo and the installer's configurator appear instead of a black screen. After the install, reboot without the USB stick: the installed system starts its graphical session with no `nomodeset` anywhere (`cat /proc/cmdline` shows the Omarchy defaults only).

records.title: Recover a locked session stranded by a plugin file change, and stop it happening
records.symptom:
The session is idle-locked. A file under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<plugin>/` then changes: `chezmoi apply` or Syncthing from another machine, a `git pull` in a plugin checkout, an agent writing files, editing a local plugin's QML, or a Python test suite dropping `__pycache__/` into the plugin directory. `journalctl --user -t omarchy-shell` shows:

```
Local plugin changed, reloading: <plugin id>
omarchy lock ... lock-stranded: recovering
omarchy lock ... lock-requested
omarchy lock ... lock-pending: screen-stabilizing
```

and it never progresses. Either Hyprland's "lockscreen app died" failsafe stays on screen with no password prompt, or the shell aborts with

```
FATAL: Tried to show lockscreen surfaces without active lock
```

(`SIGABRT`), relaunches and usually re-locks properly. `omarchy-shell lock status` reports `{"locked":true,"requested":true,"pending":true,"sessionLocked":false,"secure":true,...}`, and `omarchy-restart-shell` answers `Refusing to restart Omarchy shell while the session is locked.` Reported on 4.0.0-1, 4.0.1-1 and 4.0.2-1, with both `quickshell-git 0.3.0` and `quickshell 0.3.1-1`.
records.cause: Established in the thread by the collaborator triage against `quattro` and the quickshell sources, and by core dumps from three reporters. A plugin change triggers `reloadPlugins()`, which calls `unloadPluginServices()` in `shell/shell.qml`. On 4.0.2-1 that function destroys every plugin service unconditionally (confirmed on this machine at `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/shell.qml` lines 348 to 354), including `omarchy.lock`, which owns the live `WlSessionLock`. The lock manifest's `keepLoaded: true` was honoured for panels only. Destroying the lock client leaves the compositor's `ext-session-lock` standing (that is Hyprland's failsafe) and leaves quickshell's process-global `QSWaylandSessionLockManager::active` pointer dangling, because only `unlock()` clears it. From then on no lock attempt in that process can succeed. The rebuilt lock service reads `sessionLock.secure` through the dangling pointer: if it reads true the service returns early forever (the silent `lock-pending` stall, the shape in #6888), if it reads false it sets `locked = true` and quickshell's `qFatal` aborts the process. Only a new quickshell process can take a lock again. `omarchy-restart-shell` refuses because it tests `.secure or .requested` from that same wedged service (`/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-restart-shell` lines 29 to 35 on 4.0.2-1). The same teardown is reachable without a file write through `omarchy plugin disable omarchy.lock` or `omarchy plugin remove` while locked, which go through `_syncServices()`.
records.fix:
**The fix that landed.** PR #9485 (merged 2026-09-02, commit `d3d23fdd` on `quattro`) makes `unloadPluginServices()` keep any service whose manifest sets `keepLoaded: true`, which `omarchy.lock` does, so a plugin hot-reload no longer destroys the lock client. It is **not** in 4.0.2-1 or any earlier release. Once a release after 4.0.2 carries it:

```bash
omarchy update
grep -n serviceKeepLoaded /usr/share/omarchy/shell/shell.qml   # present once the fix has arrived
```

Still open after that merge, per the thread: `omarchy plugin disable` or `remove` while locked, and recovery of a process that has already taken the damage (PR #7169).

**Prevention on 4.0.2 and earlier.** Do not write under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` while the screen is locked. Gate sync and dotfile tools on `omarchy-hyprland-session-locked`, which exits 0 while the compositor holds a session lock (one reporter runs this as a chezmoi pre-apply hook):

```bash
if omarchy-hyprland-session-locked; then
  echo "session is locked, not touching plugins" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

**Recovery when already stranded.** From a TTY (`Ctrl+Alt+F2`) or over ssh as the session user, inside a login shell (`bash -lc`, otherwise `OMARCHY_PATH` is unset and every `omarchy` command fails). Kill the wedged shell process. `SIGKILL` cannot be caught by quickshell's crash handler, so the supervisor `omarchy-launch-shell` logs `Omarchy shell exited with status 137; relaunching.` and the fresh process re-secures the lock on its own within a few seconds, after which the password prompt works. Confirmed by one reporter on 4.0.2-1 and consistent with the source analysis that only a new process clears the dangling pointer:

```bash
pkill -9 -x quickshell
sleep 6
omarchy-shell lock status        # expect "sessionLocked":true,"secure":true
```

If the supervisor has given up (`Giving up on the Omarchy shell after 6 relaunches in under a minute.` in the journal) or you also killed `omarchy-launch-shell`, no client holds the lock any more. Clear Hyprland's failsafe and start the shell again. The session comes back **unlocked**:

```bash
hyprctl --instance 0 eval 'hl.clear_crashed_lockscreen()'
hyprctl --instance 0 dispatch 'hl.dsp.exec_cmd("omarchy-launch-shell")'
```

`hl.clear_crashed_lockscreen()` exists in Hyprland 0.56.2 (its error strings are in `/usr/bin/Hyprland` on this machine) and refuses while a client still holds the lock, which is why the kill has to come first. The failsafe text's `killall -9 hyprlock` does nothing on Omarchy 4, which has no hyprlock.
records.verify:
```bash
journalctl --user -t omarchy-shell -n 30 --no-pager    # after the relaunch: lock-requested, then secure=true
omarchy-shell lock status | jq '.sessionLocked, .secure'   # true, true
```

Then type the password at the lock screen. One reporter's journal after the kill: `lock-stranded: recovering` at 12:45:59, `secure=true` at 12:46:05, password accepted.

records.title: Stop ttfx dumping core every time the screensaver is torn down by the lock
records.symptom:
On Omarchy 4.0.0-1 with `ttfx 0.3.1-1`, idling through the screensaver into the lock (or dismissing the screensaver) leaves a `ttfx` core dump behind and a "Process crashed" notification. `coredumpctl list | grep ttfx` shows `SIGABRT` entries, one per monitor. The panic recovered from the core:

```
thread 'main' (7320) panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1166:9:
failed printing to stderr: Input/output error (os error 5)
```

Reported on Intel and AMD laptops and NVIDIA desktops, with foot and ghostty as the screensaver terminal, with `idle: {screensaver: 150, lock: 300}`.
records.cause: `ttfx`, the screensaver renderer, is painting into a terminal that the lock script or the screensaver dismiss has already closed. Its next write fails with `EIO`, it reports that error with `eprintln!`, stderr is the same dead pty, and the report itself panics. Release builds abort on panic, hence `SIGABRT` and a core. Three routes into the same abort are documented across the thread and its linked issues: the lock script killing an already running screensaver (#6762, #6764), the screensaver supervisor loop respawning a renderer into a terminal that is being closed, and the one this issue reports, the idle service starting a fresh cycle and launching a second screensaver into a lock that is still being requested. The collaborator triage confirmed that last one in source: `lockSystem()` spawns `omarchy-system-lock` as a subprocess and about a second passes before `lock-requested` is set, `startIdleCycle()` consults no lock state, and with `screensaver <= lock` the delay is 0, so any idle re-assertion in that second launches a screensaver immediately.
records.fix:
The fix is `ttfx 0.3.2` (omacom-io/ttfx#18, "Stop dumping core when the terminal goes away", merged 2026-08-17): a failed write to the tty is dropped instead of panicking, and `EIO`/`EPIPE` on the output tty ends the run quietly with exit 0. Omarchy's `[omarchy]` package repository carries `ttfx 0.3.2-1` (built 17 August 2026, confirmed on this machine).

```bash
pacman -Q ttfx      # 0.3.1-1 is affected
omarchy update
pacman -Q ttfx      # 0.3.2-1
```

The Omarchy-side race, a second screensaver launched into a pending lock, is still open: PRs #7131 and #7132 are unmerged as of 2026-09-07. With `ttfx 0.3.2` the terminal is still torn down abruptly, but the renderer exits instead of dumping core.
records.verify:
After the update, idle through the screensaver into the lock, unlock, then check that no new entry appeared:

```bash
coredumpctl list ttfx --since '-1h'
```

records.title: Screen recording never starts on a Pascal NVIDIA card: 'Driver does not support the required nvenc API version. Required: 13.1 Found: 13.0'
records.symptom:
`omarchy screenrecord` (every variant: fullscreen, region, with or without audio or webcam) does nothing. The bar's recording indicator never turns on and no file appears in `~/Videos`. With `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DEBUG=true` set, `/tmp/omarchy-screenrecord.log` ends with:

```
gsr info: using h264 encoder because a codec was not specified
[h264_nvenc @ 0x557b3650a880] ignoring invalid SAR: 0/0
[h264_nvenc @ 0x557b3650a880] Driver does not support the required nvenc API version. Required: 13.1 Found: 13.0
[h264_nvenc @ 0x557b3650a880] The minimum required Nvidia driver for nvenc is 610.00 or newer
gsr error: Could not open video codec: Function not implemented
```

Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 with a GeForce GTX 1070 Ti on `nvidia-580xx-dkms 580.178.04` and `gpu-screen-recorder 6.0.0-1`. A second reporter hit the same two `h264_nvenc` lines from Kdenlive's NVENC export presets on a Quadro P1000 with the same driver, and the same message comes from any program that encodes through the system `ffmpeg`.
records.cause: Named by the gpu-screen-recorder author in the thread. ffmpeg 9.0 raised the minimum NVENC API it will talk to from 13.0 to 13.1. API 13.1 needs driver 610.00 or newer, and Pascal cards (GTX 10 series, Quadro P series) are stuck on the legacy `nvidia-580xx` branch, which only reports 13.0. `omarchy-capture-screenrecording` passes `-fallback-cpu-encoding yes` to `gpu-screen-recorder` (line 191 of the script on this machine), but before 6.0.1 that option only checked whether the GPU supports NVENC, not whether ffmpeg accepts the driver's API version, so the recorder died opening the codec instead of falling back to software encoding. The author added an ffmpeg NVENC version check in gpu-screen-recorder 6.0.1 so the fallback fires, and made the `-Dffmpeg_static=true` build option (a bundled ffmpeg patched to negotiate the NVENC API at runtime) the default for later releases. Programs that use the system ffmpeg, such as Kdenlive, mpv and OBS, are not helped by either change.
records.fix:
1. Check the recorder version. 6.0.1 or newer carries the fallback fix. On Omarchy 4 update through the supported path:

```bash
pacman -Q gpu-screen-recorder    # 6.0.0-1 is affected, 6.0.1-1 or newer has the fallback
omarchy update
```

On plain Arch, `sudo pacman -Syu`. Arch's `extra` repository has shipped 6.0.1 since 2026-08-20 and 6.1.0 since 2026-09-02.

2. Until the update lands, or if it still fails, force software encoding when calling the recorder directly. The Omarchy wrapper has no option for this, so run `gpu-screen-recorder` yourself. Replace `DP-2` with your monitor name from `hyprctl monitors`:

```bash
gpu-screen-recorder -w DP-2 -encoder cpu -f 60 -o ~/Videos/recording.mp4
# stop with Ctrl+C, or from another terminal:
pkill -SIGINT -f gpu-screen-recorder
```

The reporter confirmed `-encoder cpu` produces a valid clip on the same card and driver.

3. Kdenlive, mpv, OBS and anything else that uses the system `ffmpeg` cannot use NVENC on a Pascal card with ffmpeg 9 at all. Pick a software encoder (x264 or x265) in those programs. No driver update will change this: the 580xx branch is the last one for Pascal.
records.verify:
```bash
pacman -Q gpu-screen-recorder            # 6.0.1-1 or newer
OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_DEBUG=true omarchy screenrecord --fullscreen
```

The bar's recording indicator turns on, a file appears in `~/Videos`, and `/tmp/omarchy-screenrecord.log` no longer contains `Could not open video codec`.

records.title: Fingerprint unlock fails after every suspend: fprintd reports 'Cannot run while suspended'
records.symptom:
The fingerprint reader unlocks the Omarchy lock screen fine after boot. After the machine suspends and resumes, the lock screen's fingerprint prompt hangs or fails instantly, and only the password gets you in. `sudo` with a fingerprint keeps working. In the journal:

```
fprintd[PID]: Device reported an error during verify: Cannot run while suspended.
```

Some readers log `transfer timed out` instead. The lock screen then retries fingerprint PAM roughly four times a second, so the journal fills with lines like these until you type the password:

```
omarchy-shell[...]: Error while authenticating: "Authentication service cannot retrieve authentication info" (code 9)
```

Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 through 4.0.2-1 with Goodix MOC readers (`27c6:609c`, `27c6:634c`, `27c6:659c`) on Intel Meteor Lake, Panther Lake and Framework AMD laptops, fprintd 1.94.5-2, libfprint 1.94.100-1, both s2idle and deep sleep.
records.cause:
Established in the thread and confirmed against the source by the repository's review bot. `omarchy-system-sleep-monitor` runs under `systemd-inhibit --what=sleep --mode=delay` and locks the screen inside that delay window (the `exec systemd-inhibit` block at the end of `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor` on this machine). As soon as the lock goes secure, the lock plugin starts fingerprint auth, which D-Bus-activates `fprintd` while logind's sleep operation is already in flight. logind refuses fprintd its own sleep-delay inhibitor:

```
fprintd[...]: Failed to install a sleep delay inhibitor: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.login1.OperationInProgress: The operation inhibition has been requested for is already running
```

Without that inhibitor fprintd is never told to release the reader before suspend and never receives the wake-up signal after it, so the same daemon survives resume holding a dead USB handle and refuses every verify until it exits on its own idle timeout, which can be hours later. `sudo` works because it activates fprintd outside any sleep transition. The ~4 Hz retry storm is a separate lock-screen defect (issues 7172 and 7176) that makes this one louder.
records.fix:
Stop `fprintd` around every sleep so the next authentication activates a fresh daemon. `fprintd.service` is D-Bus activated (`Type=dbus`, `BusName=net.reactivated.Fprint`), so stopping it is enough and nothing needs restarting. The hook must live in `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/`: systemd 261 scans no other directory, and a copy in `/etc/systemd/system-sleep/` never runs. It must also be executable, or it is ignored with nothing logged.

```bash
sudo tee /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/fprintd-reset >/dev/null <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Stop fprintd on the way into and out of sleep so the lock screen never
# reuses a daemon that was activated inside logind's sleep-delay window.
case "$1" in
  pre|post) systemctl stop fprintd.service 2>/dev/null || true ;;
esac
exit 0
EOF
sudo chmod +x /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/fprintd-reset
```

The same applies on plain Arch with any Hyprland lock screen that starts fingerprint auth before suspend. The directory is package-independent, so the file survives updates, but it is not owned by any package: note it somewhere or you will forget it exists.

If you only need to recover right now without the hook:

```bash
systemctl restart fprintd.service
```

Upstream has three open pull requests for this as of 2026-09-07 (7158 and 9868 ship a hook of this shape, 9919 delays fingerprint checks until after resume). None has merged, so the hook is the fix until one does.
records.verify:
```bash
systemctl show fprintd.service -p MainPID     # note the PID (0 if not running)
systemctl suspend
# after resume:
systemctl show fprintd.service -p MainPID     # different PID, or 0 until the lock screen uses it
journalctl -b -u fprintd.service | grep -c 'Cannot run while suspended'   # stays at 0 from now on
```

The reporter who moved the hook into `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/` confirmed fprintd's PID changed across the next suspend, and the original reporter confirmed a restarted fprintd authenticates on the lock screen immediately.

records.title: Omarchy installer dies at 'mounting the ESP failed (exit 32)' with a SQUASHFS superblock error
records.symptom:
Installing Omarchy 4.0.0 from the ISO into free space, alongside Windows or alongside other data. The installer creates the LUKS container, the btrfs filesystem and its subvolumes, then stops at the last disk step:

```
mount: /mnt/boot: fsconfig() failed: Can't find a SQUASHFS superblock on nvme0n1p3.
       dmesg(1) may have more information after failed mount system call.
mounting the ESP failed (exit 32)
```

The original reporter had Windows on one NVMe drive and the free space on a second one. Four more people hit the identical message, including with the free space on the same disk as Windows.
records.cause: Named in the pull request that fixes it (omarchy-iso 111, open and unmerged as of 2026-09-07). The installer's `configurator` script formats the new ESP with `mkfs.fat` and immediately mounts it with `mount "$efi_dev" ...`, with no `-t vfat`. Without a filesystem type, `mount` probes the device, and on these systems the probe runs before udev has re-read the freshly written partition or picks the wrong type, so the kernel tries SQUASHFS and fails with exit code 32. The `detect_windows_esp()` function has the same bare `mount -o ro` for probing existing ESPs. The current `quattro` branch of `omacom/omarchy-iso` still has both lines (`configs/airootfs/root/configurator` lines 396 and 773), so every published ISO carries the defect.
records.fix:
Patch the installer script inside the live environment and rerun it. Nothing has been written to your real disk that a rerun does not redo, and the edit is lost on reboot, so do it in the same live session that failed.

1. When the installer drops you at a shell, you are in `/root` on the live ISO. Open the script:

```bash
ls -la
nano configurator
```

2. Find the block that formats and mounts the ESP (search for `mounting the ESP`):

```bash
disk_step "creating the ESP filesystem on $efi_dev" mkfs.fat -F32 -n OMARCHY_EFI "$efi_dev"
disk_step "mounting the ESP" mount "$efi_dev" /mnt"$esp_mount_in_target"
```

Change it to:

```bash
disk_step "creating the ESP filesystem on $efi_dev" mkfs.fat -F32 -n OMARCHY_EFI "$efi_dev"
udevadm settle
sleep 2
disk_step "mounting the ESP" mount -t vfat "$efi_dev" /mnt"$esp_mount_in_target"
```

3. In `detect_windows_esp()`, change:

```bash
if mount -o ro "$p" "$tmp_mp" 2>/dev/null; then
```

to:

```bash
if mount -t vfat -o ro "$p" "$tmp_mp" 2>/dev/null; then
```

4. Save, unmount what the failed run left behind, and start the installer again:

```bash
umount -R /mnt 2>/dev/null
./.automated_script.sh
```

Answer the installer's questions again exactly as before. Three later reporters confirmed this sequence completes the install.
records.verify:
The installer passes `mounting the ESP` and continues to package installation. After the first boot into Omarchy:

```bash
findmnt /boot            # FSTYPE vfat, SOURCE the new ESP
lsblk -f | grep OMARCHY_EFI
```
records.danger: Rerunning the installer reformats the partitions it created in the free space. Confirm the target disk and partition on the installer's summary screen before accepting: on a two-disk machine the free space and the Windows ESP are on different drives, and picking the wrong one destroys Windows.

records.title: Zed install ends with '[WARN] Could not determine current Omarchy theme' from omazed
records.symptom:
Installing Zed from the Omarchy menu (Install > Editor > Zed, which runs `omarchy-install-editor-zed`) installs the `zed` and `omazed` packages, then `omazed setup` prints:

```
[INFO] Setting up Omazed for user: user

[INFO] Removed old omazed hook
[SUCCESS] ✓ Omarchy hook configured
[WARN] Could not determine current Omarchy theme
```

Zed opens with its default theme and does not follow the Omarchy theme. Running `omazed setup` again gives the same warning. Reported on a fresh Omarchy Quattro (4.0.0) install.
records.cause: Named by the person who fixed it in the thread and confirmed in the omazed commit. omazed 2.0.x read the active theme from `~/.config/omarchy/current/theme`, which is where Omarchy 3 kept it. Omarchy 4 keeps state under `~/.local/state/omarchy/`, so the current theme is `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme` (present on this machine) and the old path does not exist. omazed commit 302cd396 (2026-08-15, released as 2.1.0) checks the Omarchy 4 path first and falls back to the Omarchy 3 path. The AUR package builds from the repository's current tag, so anyone who installed omazed before the AUR package moved to 2.1.0 has the old code.
records.fix:
Rebuild omazed from the AUR at 2.1.0 or newer, then run its setup again. From the Omarchy menu use Install > AUR, search for `omazed` and install it (this runs `yay -S aur/omazed`), or from a terminal:

```bash
yay -S --noconfirm aur/omazed
pacman -Q omazed          # 2.1.0-1 or newer
omazed setup
```

The reporter confirmed this fixed the warning. Plain Arch users of omazed are not affected unless they also run Omarchy 4.
records.verify:
```bash
omazed setup              # ends without the [WARN] line
ls ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml
```

Change the Omarchy theme (Super+Ctrl+Shift+Space) and Zed's theme changes with it.

records.title: YouTube and other AV1 video shows shifted colours or pixelated blocks on AMD graphics (linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-1)
records.symptom: After updating, or on a fresh Omarchy 4.0.0-1 install, videos on YouTube in Firefox and Chromium show rectangular areas with the wrong colours or tint, sometimes pixelated. Lower resolutions such as 480p look fine, higher AV1 streams do not. The corruption is in the decoded frames, so it shows in screenshots too. Reported on a Ryzen 7 8745HS with Radeon 780M, a Ryzen 5 7640U with Radeon 760M, and a Radeon RX 9070 XT. `pacman -Q linux-firmware-amdgpu` shows `20260810-1`.
records.cause: Established in the thread and in issue 7514. `linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-1` carries an AMD GPU firmware regression that corrupts hardware AV1 decoding. Arch fixed it in `20260810-2` on 2026-08-15, but the Omarchy stable mirror had snapshotted the repositories with `-1` and stayed there until 2026-08-24. The Firefox and Chromium hardware decoders use the firmware through VA-API, which is why every browser was affected and why disabling hardware decoding in Firefox alone did not help one reporter.
records.fix:
Update. The stable mirror has carried `linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-2` since 2026-08-24, and the workstation this record was checked on has it installed.

Omarchy 4:

```bash
omarchy update
pacman -Q linux-firmware-amdgpu     # 20260810-2 or newer
```

Plain Arch:

```bash
sudo pacman -Syu
```

Reboot afterwards: GPU firmware is loaded when the `amdgpu` module initialises, so the running session keeps the old firmware until then.

If you cannot update yet, one reporter on a Radeon 760M confirmed that turning off AV1 in Firefox stops the corruption: open `about:config`, set `media.av1.enabled` to `false`, and YouTube falls back to VP9. That is a workaround, not the fix.
records.verify:
```bash
pacman -Q linux-firmware-amdgpu     # 20260810-2
```

After a reboot, play a 1080p or 4K YouTube video: colours are stable and no blocks appear. One reporter on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 confirmed the update alone fixed it.

records.title: Finish the Copy URL migration that re-prompts at every login and does nothing on Yes
records.symptom:
After upgrading Omarchy 3 to Quattro (reported on 4.0.0-1), a pending-migration notification appears at every login. Running the migration shows the prompt `Close the browser windows to repair the Copy URL shortcut, then continue`. Choosing Yes does nothing and the prompt comes straight back, even with every browser window closed. On decline the migration prints:

```
A running browser would undo the Copy URL shortcut repair.
Close the browser windows, then run: omarchy-migrate
```

Reported with Brave, and confirmed by a second reporter with Vivaldi and Chromium.
records.cause: The thread established that stale browser lock files were the blocker: `SingletonLock`, `SingletonCookie` and `SingletonSocket` left in the browser's config directory by a browser that had exited without cleaning them up. The migration is `migrations/1786643346.sh`, which repairs the Copy URL extension shortcut in Chromium-family `Preferences` files. Read on this machine (omarchy 4.0.2-1), its `profile_open` check treats a profile as open when `SingletonLock` exists, including as a dangling symlink, or `SingletonSocket` exists, and it loops on the confirm prompt until no affected profile is open. A stale lock therefore looks like a running browser forever, so the migration never completes and `omarchy-migrate-notify` reports it as pending at every login.
records.fix:
Close every Chromium-family browser, then delete the stale lock files for the browsers you have. The two confirmed commands from the thread, for Chromium plus Vivaldi and for Brave plus Chromium:

```bash
rm -v ~/.config/chromium/SingletonLock ~/.config/chromium/SingletonCookie ~/.config/chromium/SingletonSocket ~/.config/vivaldi/SingletonLock ~/.config/vivaldi/SingletonCookie ~/.config/vivaldi/SingletonSocket
```

```bash
rm -vf ~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/Singleton{Lock,Cookie,Socket} ~/.config/chromium/Singleton{Lock,Cookie,Socket}
```

The same three files live under the profile root of any other Chromium-family browser the migration scans: `~/.config/google-chrome`, `~/.config/microsoft-edge`, `~/.config/opera`, `~/.config/helium` and the beta and nightly variants. Then run the migration again:

```bash
omarchy-migrate
```

Only delete the files while the browser is not running. A live browser owns them and removing them lets a second instance start against the same profile.
records.verify: `omarchy-migrate --pending` prints nothing, and no migration notification appears at the next login. Both reporters confirmed `omarchy-migrate` ran through once the lock files were gone.

records.title: Fix blocky colour corruption in AV1 video on Radeon RX 9000 after linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-1
records.symptom: After an update, higher-resolution AV1 streams (YouTube `av01.0.12M.08` at 4K) show rectangular blocks of wrong colours in Firefox, Chromium and Brave on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. 480p AV1 streams are fine. The corruption is visible in screenshots, so it is in the decoded frames rather than the display path. Reported on the Omarchy stable channel with `linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-1` and Mesa 26.1.7-1, kernel 7.1.8-arch1-3. The reporter had upgraded from 3.8.4, and a second reporter confirmed on Omarchy 4.0.0.
records.cause: A firmware change in `linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-1` altered how the AV1 decoder on RDNA4 (gfx12, Navi 48) reads the quantizer matrix parameters, so frames decoded in hardware come out wrong. Two fixes exist upstream and either one is enough: Arch's `linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-2` (published 2026-08-15) reverts the behaviour, and Mesa merge request 43787, `radv/video: Fix AV1 decode qmatrix params`, merged 2026-08-17 and shipped in Mesa 26.1.8, adapts the driver to the new firmware. The Omarchy stable mirror had snapshotted `core` on 14 August, one day before the fixed firmware, so stable users got the broken build for a week. Stable picked up 20260810-2 on 2026-08-21.
records.fix:
Omarchy 4:

```bash
omarchy update
```

The stable mirror has served `linux-firmware-amdgpu 20260810-2` since 2026-08-21 and Arch has shipped Mesa 26.2.x since, so a current update carries both fixes. Do not pull a single package with `pacman -Sy`.

Plain Arch:

```bash
sudo pacman -Syu
```

Until the update lands, the confirmed stopgap is to disable hardware video decoding in the browser. For Chromium and Brave, launch with `--disable-accelerated-video-decode`. The first reporter found that turning off hardware decoding in Firefox did not help on his machine, so treat the Firefox side as unconfirmed.
records.verify:
```bash
pacman -Q linux-firmware-amdgpu mesa
```

Expect `20260810-2` or later and Mesa `26.1.8` or later. Then reload the 4K AV1 stream with hardware decoding on. The reporter confirmed the blocks were gone after the firmware update, and the second reporter confirmed the same with only Mesa 26.1.8 and the old firmware.

records.title: Fix the free-space install failing with 'mounting the ESP failed (exit 32)' on a disk with only data partitions
records.symptom:
Installing Omarchy 4.0.0 with the installer's free space option (alongside existing data) on a disk that holds a data partition and unallocated space but no EFI System Partition fails at `Creating Btrfs filesystem and subvolumes`:

```
mount: /mnt/boot: fsconfig() failed: Can't find a SQUASHFS superblock on sda2.
       dmesg(1) may have more information after failed mount system call.
mounting the ESP failed (exit 32)
```

Nothing is written to the disk. Reproduced by the reporter on a laptop and a PC with an NTFS and with an ext4 data partition, and by a second reporter on a MacBook Pro 16 (T2) with NTFS and exFAT partitions and no ESP.
records.cause: Not established by a maintainer in the thread. What the thread shows is that the free-space path expects an EFI System Partition to exist on the disk and tries to mount one before creating its own, and on a disk with no ESP it mounts the wrong partition. A related report, omacom/omarchy#7867, found that the same path always creates a new 2 GB ESP labelled `omarchy-efi` and installs Limine there even when an ESP already exists, which matches the first reporter's observation that the dummy ESP he added stayed empty and could be deleted afterwards with Omarchy still booting.
records.fix:
Before running the installer, create a small EFI System Partition on the target disk from the installer's shell. The reporter used cfdisk:

1. Press Ctrl+C at the installer to reach a shell, or open a second console.
2. `cfdisk /dev/sdX` on the target disk. Create a new 256M partition in the free space, set its type to `EFI System`, write, quit.
3. Format it: `mkfs.fat -F32 /dev/sdXN`
4. Relaunch the installer and pick the free space option again.

The second reporter did the same with a 2 MB FAT partition and rebooted into the installer first. Both confirmed the install then completed into the remaining free space. The installer still creates and uses its own ESP, so the dummy can be removed afterwards. One reporter deleted it and Omarchy still booted, but that was one machine, so check `findmnt /boot` points at the installer's ESP before removing anything.
records.verify: The installer passes `Creating Btrfs filesystem and subvolumes` and finishes. After first boot, `findmnt /boot` shows the ESP the installer created, and `lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,PARTTYPENAME /dev/sdX` shows the data partition untouched.
records.danger: You are repartitioning a disk that holds data you want to keep. Double check the device name in cfdisk, only create the new partition inside the free space, and back the data partition up first. The installer path in question has a separate open report (omacom/omarchy#7867) of it creating a second ESP and Windows dropping out of the boot menu on dual-boot disks.

records.title: Fix the Bluetooth panel stuck on 'Turned Off' while bluetoothctl says Powered: yes
records.symptom: The Omarchy shell's Bluetooth panel shows `Turned Off`, its switch is unchecked, and clicking the switch does nothing. The AVAILABLE list never fills, so no new device can be paired from the panel. Underneath, Bluetooth is fully working: `bluetoothctl show` reports `Powered: yes`, `rfkill list bluetooth` shows no block, `omarchy-bluetooth-power is-on` exits 0, and `bluetoothctl scan on` finds devices. Already-paired devices can still connect and play audio. Each click on the dead switch logs another `rfkill: unblock set for type bluetooth` in the journal. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 and 4.0.1-1 with `quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7` and packaged `quickshell 0.3.1-1`, on Intel 8087:0a2b and 8087:0032, Realtek RTL8852BU, Qualcomm QCA9377 and Broadcom BCM20702 controllers. It appears either at boot, when the controller's firmware finishes loading after the shell has started, or after a suspend and resume with Bluetooth left on.
records.cause: Established in the thread by instrumented Quickshell logs from two reporters on different hardware. `Panel.qml` binds `adapter.enabled` straight to BlueZ's `org.bluez.Adapter1.Powered` through Quickshell's BluetoothAdapter object. When BlueZ re-registers `hci0` (firmware reload at boot, or on every resume for controllers that re-patch firmware), Quickshell drops the adapter object and builds a new one from the `InterfacesAdded` snapshot. That snapshot arrives with `PowerState: Enabling` and `Powered: false`, the `Powered: true` transition lands in the gap before the new object's `PropertiesChanged` subscription is live, and Quickshell never issues a `GetAll` for `org.bluez` to reconcile. The panel then holds `false` for as long as `Powered` stays `true`. Because `toggleBluetooth()` sends a direction derived from that cached value, the switch sends `on` to an adapter that is already on, which is a no-op. The defect is in Quickshell (0.3.0 and 0.3.1 share the same `src/bluetooth/` code), not in Omarchy's panel, and no fix had landed on either side when the thread was last updated.
records.fix:
Restart the shell. A fresh process takes a fresh snapshot of the adapter:

```bash
omarchy restart shell
```

Every reporter in the thread confirmed this clears it for the session. It recurs on the next boot or resume that hits the same window. To pair a device without restarting, use the CLI, which talks to BlueZ directly:

```bash
bluetoothctl scan on
bluetoothctl pair <MAC>
bluetoothctl connect <MAC>
```

Do not run `omarchy-bluetooth-power off` and `on` to unstick it: `off` sets an rfkill soft block, which BlueZ persists, and the panel still reads the cached value afterwards.
records.verify:
Before restarting, confirm the mismatch:

```bash
busctl --system get-property org.bluez /org/bluez/hci0 org.bluez.Adapter1 Powered
```

`b true` while the panel says `Turned Off` is this bug. After `omarchy restart shell` the panel shows the adapter on, the switch responds, and the AVAILABLE list fills when the panel is open.

records.title: Recover the Omarchy shell after 'undefined symbol: _ZN23QUntypedPropertyBindingC1EP23QPropertyBindingPrivate'
records.symptom:
After an `omarchy update` on 2026-08-20 or 2026-08-21 the bar, menu and notifications vanish. Hyprland itself still runs. The update ends with `Omarchy shell did not become ready after restart.`, and `omarchy restart shell` fails the same way:

```
quickshell: symbol lookup error: quickshell: undefined symbol: _ZN23QUntypedPropertyBindingC1EP23QPropertyBindingPrivate, version Qt_6
```

```
Giving up on the Omarchy shell after 6 relaunches in under a minute.
Omarchy shell did not become ready after restart.
```

A reboot gives a black screen or a bare Hyprland session with no shell. `yay -S quickshell-git --rebuild` changes nothing because the package comes prebuilt from the `omarchy` repository. Hit on the edge, rc and stable channels on Omarchy 4.0.0-1.
records.cause: Confirmed by dhh and by the omarchybot triage on the duplicate omacom/omarchy#7634. The Omarchy package repository published `quickshell-git 0.3.0.r20.g28771c7-2`, rebuilt against `qt6-base 6.11.2`, while the rc and stable Arch mirrors still served `qt6-base 6.11.1`. Quickshell links Qt's private ABI, the `-2` build resolves that constructor at symbol version `Qt_6` and 6.11.1's `libQt6Core` exports it only at `Qt_6_PRIVATE_API`, and the PKGBUILD declared no version constraint on `qt6-base`, so pacman installed the mismatched pair without complaint. The `quickshell-check.hook` only fires when qt6-base or qt6-wayland change, which is why a transaction upgrading quickshell-git alone gave no warning. The mirrors were brought back into agreement on 2026-08-21, and Omarchy has since moved from `quickshell-git` to the packaged `quickshell` (0.3.1-1 on this machine at omarchy 4.0.2-1).
records.fix:
Get a terminal without the shell. `Super + Return` is a Hyprland binding and still works, and so does a tty. Then update again, as dhh confirmed:

```bash
omarchy update
```

Since 2026-08-21 all three Omarchy mirrors serve Qt 6.11.2 and the repository serves the matching `quickshell-git -2`, so a plain update resolves it on every channel. If the update does not restart the shell itself:

```bash
omarchy restart shell
```

The interim workaround many reporters used, downgrading to the cached `-1` build with `sudo pacman -U /var/cache/pacman/pkg/quickshell-git-0.3.0.r20.g28771c7-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`, is now the broken half: `-1` only loads against Qt 6.11.1. Anyone still holding it should run `omarchy update` rather than keep the cached package.
records.verify:
```bash
quickshell --version
omarchy-shell shell ping
```

The first prints a version instead of the symbol lookup error, and the second prints `ok`. The bar and `Super + Space` menu are back.
records.danger: Do not pin or hold `quickshell-git` or `qt6-base` to get past this. A partial upgrade of the Qt stack reproduces the same ABI mismatch in the other direction.

records.title: Fix "Codex limits unavailable" in the Agents panel after Codex CLI 0.149
records.symptom:
After Codex CLI updates from 0.148.0 to 0.149.0 or later, the Omarchy Agents panel stops showing Codex subscription limits. Local token and session statistics still display, but the limits section reads `Codex limits unavailable` with the help text `initialize`. Refreshing the panel does not recover it. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 and 4.0.1-1.

The packaged collector reproduces it:

```console
$ omarchy-agent-usage-codex --limits-only | jq '{ready,limitCount:(.limits|length),usageStatusText,authHelpText}'
{
  "ready": true,
  "limitCount": 0,
  "usageStatusText": "Codex limits unavailable",
  "authHelpText": "initialize"
}
```

Launching app-server the way the collector does shows the real error:

```console
$ codex -s read-only -a untrusted app-server
error: invalid value 'untrusted' for '--ask-for-approval <APPROVAL_POLICY>'
  [possible values: on-request, never]
```
records.cause:
Codex CLI 0.149.0 retired the `untrusted` approval policy (openai/codex#39630). The collector `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex` launched `codex -s read-only -a untrusted app-server` (line 531 in the file at tag v4.0.1), so codex exits before the RPC handshake. The collector discards app-server's stderr and reports the name of the pending RPC method, `initialize`, as the help text, which is why the panel shows a method name where an auth hint belongs. Nothing about authentication is wrong.

At the time of the reports Omarchy's own `openai-codex-bin` package was still on 0.148.0, so the people hitting this had installed Codex another way, mostly through mise. Once that package moves past 0.148.0 every install without the fix sees it.
records.fix:
The fix is PR #7649 (merged to `quattro` 2026-08-25), listed in the v4.0.2 release notes as "Fix Codex usage collection on version 0.149". Tag v4.0.1 still ships `untrusted`, tag v4.0.2 ships `on-request` at the same line. Update:

```bash
omarchy update
```

Then confirm the installed collector carries it:

```bash
grep -n '"-a"' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex
# 531:      [codex, "-s", "read-only", "-a", "on-request", "app-server"],
```

Stuck on 4.0.1 and need the panel now: change the one value in the packaged collector. Both `on-request` (what the merged PR uses) and `never` (what two reporters tested, 2/2 runs each) work, because the collector only sends `initialize`, `initialized`, `account/read` and `account/rateLimits/read` and never starts a turn.

```bash
sudo sed -i 's/"-a", "untrusted", "app-server"/"-a", "never", "app-server"/' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex
```

The file belongs to the `omarchy` package, so the next `omarchy update` overwrites the edit with the released fix, which is the intended outcome. Refresh the Agents panel afterwards. No login or credential change is needed.
records.verify:
```bash
omarchy-agent-usage-codex --limits-only | jq '{ready,limitCount:(.limits|length),usageStatusText,authHelpText}'
```

`limitCount` is 1 or more and `usageStatusText` is empty. Two reporters saw the authenticated plan plus the 5-hour and weekly windows return immediately after the change.

records.title: Fix an ISO install that fails with "failed retrieving file ... from disk" for a package in the offline mirror
records.symptom:
Installing from the Omarchy 4.0.x ISO fails part way through. During the "Installing Arch + Omarchy" (pacstrap) stage:

```
failed retrieving file 'gst-plugin-gtk-1.28.6-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst' from disk : Could not open file
ERROR: Failed to install packages to new root
```

or, on the first attempt in a boot, during "Configuring system":

```
:: File /var/cache/pacman/pkg/nvidia-utils-610.57.04-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst is corrupted
Do you want to delete it? [Y/n]  error: failed to commit transaction (invalid or corrupted package)
Failed: /usr/share/omarchy/install/hardware/nvidia.sh
```

Looking in `/var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline/` from the installer shell, the named package really is absent, and `/etc/pacman.conf` points at `Server = file:///var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline/`. Retrying in the same boot fails the same way every time, and a later retry can add `failed retrieving 'offline.db' from disk`. The network is up and unrelated. Reported on the 4.0.0 (`IMAGE_VERSION=2026.08.14`), 4.0.1 and 4.0.2 ISOs, naming `gst-plugin-gtk` (three reporters) and `nvidia-utils` (one).
records.cause:
The ISO is not missing the package. A collaborator checked the published 4.0.0 and 4.0.1 images against their own signatures and manifests and found every package in the offline mirror present with a matching sha256 (1247 and 1249 packages respectively). The failure happens between that file and pacman reading it: a bad download, a bad write to the stick, or a bad read off it.

During the install the offline mirror directory is bind-mounted as pacman's package cache, so the repository pacman fetches from and the cache it validates are the same directory. When one package fails its checksum, pacman's "File ... is corrupted. Do you want to delete it?" is answered yes by `--noconfirm` and the file is unlinked out of the mirror. The collaborator reproduced that on a clean VM with pacman 7.1.0: intact, the package installs. With 64 bytes altered, pacman reports `invalid or corrupted package (checksum)` and deletes it, and the next attempt reports the `Could not open file` error this issue was filed about. The deletion lands in the live session's RAM overlay, not on the stick, which is why every retry in the same boot fails on the missing file and a reboot brings it back.

Two reporters confirmed the media side. One was booting from a microSD card in a USB reader on a USB-C dongle: `sha512sum -c airootfs.sha512` reported a mismatch, and the install succeeded after writing the same ISO to a real USB drive. The reporter who opened the issue was on the same microSD-plus-adapter setup. The `nvidia-utils` report on the 4.0.2 ISO shows the same delete-then-missing cascade with a different package, which rules out anything specific to `gst-plugin-gtk`.

One reporter also found that when the abort lands in "Configuring system", the target is left half configured: the login step and the post-install step that replaces the offline `pacman.conf` never run, and the first boot reached an SDDM greeter that rejected the password because the theme submitted an empty username. Treat a failed install as one to redo, not one to boot.
records.fix:
Check the medium first, from a shell in the live session on a fresh boot, before starting the installer. This re-reads the whole root image off the stick and takes a few minutes:

```bash
cd /run/archiso/bootmnt/arch/x86_64 && sha512sum -c airootfs.sha512
```

A mismatch means the copy on the stick is wrong. Re-download the ISO, check it against the checksum published in the release notes (the v4.0.1 notes carry one), and write it to a different medium. A plain USB drive worked where a microSD card in a USB reader did not (confirmed by the reporter who switched, and it is the setup the original reporter was on too).

`OK` means the stick is sound. Reboot between attempts, because the deleted package stays deleted for the rest of that boot, and quote the first error after a fresh boot, since `failed retrieving file ... Could not open file` is only ever the wake of an earlier failure. `/var/log/omarchy-install.log` in the live session holds the full text.

To retry without rebooting, put the deleted package back from the read-only image, which archiso keeps mounted at `/run/archiso/airootfs` for the whole session. The collaborator tested this arrangement on a VM, no reporter has confirmed it on real media:

```bash
sudo cp /run/archiso/airootfs/var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline/gst-plugin-gtk-*.pkg.tar.zst         /var/cache/omarchy/mirror/offline/
```

Substitute whichever package the error named, then start the installer again. That `cp` is also a test, because it re-reads the same bytes off the same stick. It succeeds and the install gets past the package: a one-off misread. The install rejects the same package again with `invalid or corrupted package (checksum)`: the bytes on the stick are wrong, re-download and re-flash. The `cp` fails with an input/output error: the medium itself is failing, use another port or another stick.

Which package is named after a fresh reboot is a useful signal. The same package again means a stable fault in your copy (bad download or bad write). A different package each time means the bytes are fine and the reads are not (port, cable, card reader, or memory).

Note that the 4.0.0 ISO carries `gst-plugin-gtk-1.28.6-1` and 4.0.1 carries `-2`, so the version in the error tells you which image you booted.
records.verify: `sha512sum -c airootfs.sha512` prints `airootfs.sfs: OK`, and the installer runs through "Installing Arch + Omarchy" and "Configuring system" without naming a package. On a stick that failed the check, the same ISO written to a different USB drive installed cleanly.

records.title: Dismiss the "Process crashed" notification, or turn crash capture off
records.symptom: Omarchy 4 shows a critical "Process crashed" notification whenever a process dumps core. Clicking it launches `omarchy-agent-crash`, the AI crash diagnosis. There is no visible close control on the toast, and because the notification is critical it does not expire, so the only obvious way to make it go away is to start a diagnosis you did not want. People who crash programs on purpose (compiler and debugger work) get one after every crash. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1.
records.cause: `omarchy-crash-watch`, run by the user unit `omarchy-crash-watch.service`, sends the toast with `--urgency critical` and `--exec omarchy-agent-crash`, so a left click on the card runs the diagnosis. The close affordance on the notification card is only revealed on hover, which is the UX gap the issue is about. Two PRs are open to change that (#8980 keeps the dismiss button visible, #9010 adds a themed close button), neither merged as of 2026-09-07.
records.fix:
Dismiss one toast: right-click it. The notification card handles a right button click as a close request and a left click as the card's action (`shell/plugins/notifications/components/NotificationCard.qml` on Omarchy 4.0.2-1). One commenter reported this and it holds in the shipped source.

Stop the notifications altogether: toggle crash capture off. Two reporters confirmed the toggle exists. Either from the Omarchy menu, Super+Space, then Trigger, Toggle, Crash Capture, or from a terminal:

```bash
omarchy-toggle-crash-capture
```

That writes the flag `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/crash-capture-off`, stops `omarchy-crash-watch.service` for this session, and sends a "Crash capture disabled" notification. The unit carries `ConditionPathExists=!%h/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/crash-capture-off`, so it stays off on the next login until you run the same command again, which removes the flag and starts the watcher.

Core dumps are still captured by systemd-coredump with the watcher off. Only the notification and the one-click diagnosis go away, and `coredumpctl list` still works.
records.verify:
```bash
omarchy-toggle-enabled crash-capture-off && echo off
systemctl --user is-active omarchy-crash-watch.service
```

`off` and `inactive` while disabled. Crash something (`sleep 100 & kill -SEGV $!`) and no toast appears.

records.title: Stop the lock screen re-blanking a slow-waking monitor before it shows
records.symptom:
On Omarchy 4 (Quattro) a locked display does not wake reliably. One key press or mouse movement turns the monitor on but the lock screen never appears, or the password prompt shows for a moment and the monitor goes black again. Pressing keys or moving the mouse repeatedly eventually gets the lock screen up. `omarchy-shell` stays alive and there are no `FALLBACK` output or fatal Wayland errors in the journal, which separates this from the shell crash in #7380. The same hardware woke on the first press on Omarchy 3.

Seen on DisplayPort monitors that take more than five seconds to complete a DPMS wake: a ViewSonic VA3456-WQHD on an AMD Radeon 890M (Omarchy 4.0.0-1) and an ASUS XG32UCWMG at 3840x2160@240 on an RTX 2070 (Omarchy 4.0.0-1, issue #7399). The shipped value is unchanged on 4.0.2-1.
records.cause:
The Quickshell lock plugin blanks the display on a fixed one-shot timer. In `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml` `idleBlankTimer` has `interval: 5000` (line 416 on 4.0.2-1). `runWake()`, which runs for keyboard and pointer activity on the lock surface, starts `omarchy-system-wake` to turn DPMS on and immediately re-arms that timer. Nothing in the path observes whether the panel actually lit: `omarchy-brightness-display on` returns once `hyprctl` accepts the dispatch, not when the monitor shows a frame. A monitor whose DisplayPort wake handshake takes longer than five seconds is therefore blanked again before it becomes visible. Every keystroke re-arms the countdown, which is why repeated input eventually wins. A collaborator confirmed this reading against the source, and the reporter's controlled test (cloning the plugin and changing only the interval) confirmed it on hardware. A second user in #7399 fixed the same symptom the same way. The original reporter of #7399 saw no change at 30 seconds, so a second re-blank path may exist on some hardware.

PR #7643, which makes the interval configurable as `idle.blank` in `shell.json`, is open and unmerged as of 2026-09-07.
records.fix:
Clone the built-in lock plugin into your config and raise the interval. Cloning switches the shell to your copy and routes the lock IPC calls to it, so nothing else changes:

```bash
omarchy plugin clone omarchy.lock
```

That creates `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<username>.lock/` (for user `dhh`, `dhh.lock`). Edit `Service.qml` in that directory and change the one line:

```qml
    interval: 5000
```

to

```qml
    interval: 15000
```

15000 worked for the ViewSonic reporter, 20000 for the #7399 commenter. Saving a file under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` reloads plugin code automatically. If it does not, force it:

```bash
omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins
```

The clone stops tracking updates to the built-in lock plugin, so remove it once a release makes the interval configurable or fixes the race:

```bash
omarchy plugin remove <username>.lock
```

Removing an active clone switches the shell back to the built-in `omarchy.lock`.

If raising the interval changes nothing, this is not your cause. The #7399 reporter saw no difference at 30 seconds, and a lock screen that never appears alongside `Got removal for monitor "FALLBACK"` in the journal is #7380 instead.
records.verify:
```bash
omarchy-system-lock
```

Wait for the monitor to enter standby, then press Shift once. The monitor wakes and the lock screen stays visible without further input. `omarchy plugin list` shows `<username>.lock` enabled in place of `omarchy.lock`.

records.title: Fix the Agents panel Codex tab showing "Codex limits unavailable" with the word "initialize"
records.symptom:
The Codex tab of the omarchy-shell Agents panel (the bar's AI Agents plugin) shows a red card containing only the word `initialize` where the plan line and limit meters should be. Local token statistics still appear and the Claude tab works. `codex login status` and `codex doctor` report a healthy login. Running the collector by hand returns:

```bash
omarchy-agent-usage-codex --limits-only | jq '{tierLabel, limits, usageStatusText, authHelpText}'
```

```json
{
  "tierLabel": "",
  "limits": [],
  "usageStatusText": "Codex limits unavailable",
  "authHelpText": "initialize"
}
```

Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 and 4.0.1-1 with codex-cli 0.149.0 and 0.149.1 (installed through mise), by five separate reporters across four threads.
records.cause:
Established in the thread and confirmed by the merged fix. `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex` starts the Codex app-server at line 531 with:

```
codex -s read-only -a untrusted app-server
```

codex-cli 0.149.0 removed `untrusted` as an `--ask-for-approval` value and accepts only `on-request` and `never`, so the process exits with status 2 before speaking JSON-RPC:

```
error: invalid value 'untrusted' for '--ask-for-approval <APPROVAL_POLICY>'
  [possible values: on-request, never]
```

The collector discards stderr, sees EOF on the closed pipe, raises `TimeoutError("initialize")` from `rpc_request()` (line 495), and the handler writes `str(exc)` into `authHelpText` (line 561), so the panel renders the bare RPC method name. Omarchy 4.0.1-1 still shipped the stale value even though the fix had merged. On this workstation, omarchy 4.0.2-1, line 531 reads `-a on-request`, so 4.0.2-1 carries the fix.
records.fix:
The fix is PR #7649, merged 2026-08-25 as commit 4cd8a08, which changes the approval policy to `on-request`. It is in the omarchy package from 4.0.2-1.

**Omarchy 4 (4.0.1-1 or older):** update, then refresh the collector cache:

```bash
omarchy update
omarchy agent usage-update --force codex
```

**Interim, if you cannot update yet:** make the same one-line change the merged commit makes. The file is owned by the omarchy package, so the next update overwrites it with the fixed copy, which is what you want.

```bash
sudo sed -i '531s/"-a", "untrusted"/"-a", "on-request"/' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex
grep -n '"-a"' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex
omarchy agent usage-update --force codex
```

Reporters in #7842, #7997 and #8032 verified `never` works equally well for this path, since the collector only calls `initialize`, `account/read` and `account/rateLimits/read` and never starts a model turn. One reporter in #7873 pinned codex-cli back to 0.148.0 instead, the last version accepting `untrusted`, but nobody else confirmed that route.

**Plain Arch:** does not apply, the collector is part of Omarchy.
records.verify:
```bash
codex -s read-only -a on-request app-server </dev/null; echo "exit $?"
omarchy-agent-usage-codex --limits-only | jq '{tierLabel, limits, usageStatusText, authHelpText}'
```

The first command must not print `invalid value`. The second returns a non-empty `limits` list with `primary` and `secondary` windows and a plan type such as `plus`, and the Codex tab of the Agents panel shows the plan line and meters after the next refresh.

records.title: Fix a black desktop with a working cursor in a VMware guest (omarchy-shell cannot use vmwgfx DMA-BUF buffers)
records.symptom: Omarchy installs cleanly in a VMware guest (reported with Windows 10 and Ubuntu hosts, VMware 26H1). After the login password is accepted the screen is black or dark grey with only the mouse cursor visible. Hyprland itself is running: `Super + Enter` opens a terminal and the browser launches, but there is no bar, no wallpaper, and `Super + Space` does nothing. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0 in August 2026, with one later report on 4.0.1.
records.cause: Diagnosed by the reporter who found the fix, not by a maintainer. VMware's `vmwgfx` driver advertises a DMA-BUF modifier that Qt Quick cannot use. omarchy-shell is a Quickshell (Qt Quick) client, so when it creates its rendering buffers Hyprland rejects the `wl_surface.attach`, and the shell that draws the bar, wallpaper and menus never appears. The compositor and non-Qt clients are unaffected, which is why a terminal still opens. One reporter also found the VM needed `Accelerate 3D Graphics` enabled in VMware's display settings before the fix worked. A separate open issue, #7918, covers the invisible cursor on the same driver.
records.fix:
Run Quickshell's Qt Quick scene graph on the software rasterizer. `hl.env` in the Hyprland config exports the variable to every client Hyprland launches, which includes omarchy-shell.

If you cannot get to a terminal, log in, then press `Ctrl+Alt+F2` for a TTY. `nano` is not installed on the reported systems, so use `nvim` or `vim`.

In `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, find:

```lua
dofile((os.getenv("OMARCHY_PATH") or "/usr/share/omarchy") .. "/default/hypr/bootstrap.lua")
```

and add immediately after it:

```lua
-- VMware compatibility: avoid invalid Qt Quick DMA-BUF attachments.
hl.env("QT_QUICK_BACKEND", "software")
```

Then reboot, or log out and back in, so omarchy-shell is restarted with the new environment. The original reporter used `hyprctl reload` and saw the desktop come up, and two further reporters confirmed the same edit fixed their guests, one after a reboot.

Before powering the VM on, in VMware's VM Settings, Display, enable `Accelerate 3D Graphics`.

**Plain Arch:** the variable is the same for any Qt Quick client on vmwgfx. Set `QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software` in the environment of whatever launches the Qt application.
