records.verify: After logging back in the bar, wallpaper and `Super + Space` menu appear. From a terminal, `hyprctl clients -j | jq -r '.[].class'` lists the shell, and `cat /proc/$(pgrep -o quickshell)/environ | tr '\0' '\n' | grep QT_QUICK_BACKEND` prints `QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software`.

records.title: Fix Grok Bot installed from Install > AI failing with HTTP 404 (omarchy/grok-bot 0.18.0 is too old)
records.symptom: Grok Bot installed through the Omarchy menu (Install > AI > Grok Bot, which runs `omarchy-pkg-add grok-bot`) does not work. The 0.18.0 client's local daemon restart-loops and every request to Grok Bot's computer API returns `http_404`. There is no in-app updater on Linux. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 on 2026-08-24.

Cursor floors the Grok Bot desktop computer API at client 0.24.0 (`backend_min_version`) and changed the noVNC token scheme at 0.20.0, so the 0.18.0 build in the Omarchy package repository can no longer talk to the service. The Omarchy menu entry is correct. The package it installs was stale.
records.fix:
The fix is omarchy-pkgs PR #198, merged 2026-08-24, which repackages Grok Bot 0.24.0. The stable package repository at `pkgs.omarchy.org` served `grok-bot-0.24.0-1` when checked on 2026-09-07, so an ordinary update pulls it in.

**Omarchy 4:**

```bash
omarchy update
```

If Grok Bot was never installed, or you removed it, install it through Install > AI > Grok Bot, or directly:

```bash
omarchy-pkg-add grok-bot
```

0.24.0 renamed the binary from `sand` to `grok-bot`. The package keeps `/usr/bin/sand` as a compatibility symlink and ships `grok-bot.desktop`, so launcher entries keep working.

**Plain Arch:** the `grok-bot` package exists only in the Omarchy repository. Elsewhere, install the 0.24.0 Linux build from Cursor's downloads yourself.
records.verify:
```bash
pacman -Q grok-bot
ls -l /usr/bin/grok-bot /usr/bin/sand
```

records.title: Fix 'This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals' from the Gemini default agent
records.symptom:
Omarchy menu > Setup > Defaults > Agent > Gemini installs `gemini` through mise, writes it as the default agent and launches it. The browser sign-in completes, then the terminal fails:

```
Failed to sign in. Message: This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code
Assist for individuals. To continue using Gemini, please migrate to the
Antigravity suite of products: https://antigravity.google
```

`SUPER + SHIFT + CTRL + A` then launches a CLI that fails to sign in every time. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 with gemini-cli 0.56.0, and still present on stable 4.0.2-1, where the menu still offers Gemini and `omarchy-default-agent` accepts `gemini` but not `agy`.
records.cause: Google stopped serving Gemini CLI requests for individual Google accounts (free, AI Pro and Ultra) on 2026-06-18 and withdrew the Login with Google path for them. Gemini CLI now needs a paid API key or an enterprise licence. The Omarchy menu entry still installs and selects it. The maintainer replaced Gemini with Antigravity CLI (`agy`) in PR #6900, merged into `quattro` on 2026-08-20, but that change was not in the stable 4.0.2-1 package. The backport to stable is tracked separately in PR #8952.
records.fix:
On a build that carries PR #6900 (the `quattro` branch from 2026-08-20 onward), run the update and choose the new entry. Migration `1786719479` installs the `agy` lazy stub through mise and rewrites a `gemini` default to `agy`:

```bash
omarchy update
```

Then Omarchy menu > Setup > Defaults > Agent > **Antigravity**, or from a terminal:

```bash
omarchy-default-agent agy
```

```bash
omarchy-mise-install antigravity-cli agy
agy
```

records.title: Fix the Omarchy shell crash-looping under VMware with 3D acceleration: 'invalid arguments for wl_surface.attach'
records.symptom:
Omarchy 4.0.x as a VMware Workstation guest with **Accelerate 3D graphics** enabled boots into Hyprland, but the desktop is a uniform dark fill with only the cursor: no bar, no wallpaper. `omarchy-launch-shell` relaunches the shell five times in under a minute and gives up. Running the shell by hand with `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` shows the fatal protocol error:

```
[Default Queue] -> zwp_linux_buffer_params_v1#34.create_immed(new id wl_buffer#46, 1718, 52, 875713089, 0)
[Default Queue] -> wl_surface#42.attach(wl_buffer#46, 0, 0)
[Display Queue] wl_display#1.error(wl_display#1, 1, "invalid arguments for wl_surface#42.attach")
WARN: The Wayland connection experienced a fatal error: Invalid argument
```

Hyprland logs `unknown object (61), message attach(?oii)` and `error in client communication`. Other GPU-rendered clients hit the same error: `mpv --vo=gpu`, and XWayland dies when an X11 app such as Spotify starts (`XWAYLAND: wl_display#1: error 1: invalid arguments for wl_surface#18.attach`). Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0 through 4.0.2 with Hyprland 0.56.2, Mesa 26.2.1, `vmwgfx` 2.21.0, VMware SVGA II `15ad:0405`.
records.cause: The thread establishes the failure point, not a maintainer verdict. Mesa's `svga` driver advertises no DMA-BUF render modifiers for the scanout formats while `vmwgfx` KMS advertises only `LINEAR`, so a GL-backed Qt Quick client hands Hyprland a dmabuf whose modifier the compositor rejects at `wl_surface.attach`, a fatal protocol error. Qt exits without a signal, so Quickshell's crash handler never runs and the supervisor sees a bare exit. The compositor itself is not affected: a Hyprland with no env overrides composites on `vmwgfx` and falls back to implicit modifiers (`GBM: Allocating with modifiers failed, falling back to implicit`). A minimal `qml6` window reproduces it with no Omarchy involved. Upstream discussion is hyprwm/Hyprland #12966. One reporter posted a Hyprland source patch that closes vmwgfx surface handles with `DRM_VMW_UNREF_SURFACE`, which nobody else confirmed.
records.fix:
Make the shell render with the Qt Quick software rasterizer, so its surface is a shm buffer and no dmabuf is created. The compositor stays on the GPU. Two reporters confirmed this on 4.0.2. Put it in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` after `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`:

```lua
hl.env("QT_QUICK_BACKEND", "software")
```

If XWayland applications (Spotify, Electron apps forced to X11) still kill XWayland, also disable glamor (one reporter, tested only together with the line above):

```lua
hl.env("XWAYLAND_NO_GLAMOR", "1")
```

Log out and back in. `hl.env` only reaches processes started after the session begins, so `hyprctl reload` is not enough.

Do not use `QSG_RHI_BACKEND=software`. Two reporters found it changes nothing, and the journal on the installed Qt stack says why:

```
Unknown key "software" for QSG_RHI_BACKEND, falling back to default backend.
```

`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` also stops the crash, but it forces the whole session, compositor included, onto llvmpipe (Hyprland idle CPU measured at about 12% against 4% with the Qt-only switch), and one reporter on a fresh 4.0.2 install got no shell with it at all. `QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_HARDWARE_INTEGRATION=1` does not help.

The cost is that XWayland applications render in software. One reporter measured Spotify at about 60% of a core with `XWAYLAND_NO_GLAMOR=1`.
records.verify:
After a fresh login the bar and wallpaper appear and the shell stays up. Count supervisor relaunches, which should be 0:

```bash
journalctl -b -t omarchy-shell | grep -c 'exited with status'
```

The journal shows `Disabling glamor and dri3 support, XWAYLAND_NO_GLAMOR is set` if that variable was added.

records.title: Make Files (Nautilus) 'Set as Wallpaper' change the Omarchy background
records.symptom:
Right-click an image in Files (Nautilus) and choose Set as Wallpaper (Set as Background on Nautilus 50). Nothing changes. `journalctl --user` shows:

```
org.gnome.Nautilus: Failed to set wallpaper via portal:
GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownMethod:
No such interface "org.freedesktop.portal.Wallpaper"
on object at path /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop
```

Reported on Omarchy 4.0.1-1 and 4.0.2-1 with Nautilus 50.2.2-1.
records.cause: Nautilus 50 asks the XDG desktop portal to set the wallpaper. The session's portal backends are `xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland` 1.4.1 (Screenshot, ScreenCast, GlobalShortcuts, InputCapture) and `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` 1.15.3 (FileChooser, Settings and others). Neither implements `org.freedesktop.portal.Wallpaper`, so the call fails before anything is written. Installing `xdg-desktop-portal-gnome` would not help: it writes GNOME's gsettings key, and nothing in Omarchy reads it. Omarchy's background is the `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/background` symlink drawn by `omarchy-shell`, set through `omarchy-theme-bg-set`. A contributor said a fix would need Omarchy to either implement the Wallpaper portal or hide the dead menu item. Neither had landed when the issue was closed.
records.fix:
Add a Files context-menu item that calls Omarchy's own command. `nautilus-python` is in Omarchy's base package set (`install/omarchy-base.packages`), so no install is needed. This extension was posted by one user and confirmed working by the reporter on 4.0.1-1:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/nautilus-python/extensions
cat > ~/.local/share/nautilus-python/extensions/omarchy-background.py <<'EOF'
import gi

gi.require_version("Nautilus", "4.1")
from gi.repository import Gio, GObject, Nautilus


class OmarchyBackgroundExtension(GObject.GObject, Nautilus.MenuProvider):
    def get_file_items(self, files):
        if len(files) != 1:
            return []

        selected = files[0]
        location = selected.get_location()
        path = location.get_path() if location else None
        mime_type = selected.get_mime_type() or ""
        if not path or not mime_type.startswith("image/"):
            return []

        item = Nautilus.MenuItem(
            name="OmarchyBackgroundExtension::set_background",
            label="Set as Omarchy Background",
        )
        item.connect("activate", self._set_background, path)
        return [item]

    def get_background_items(self, _current_folder):
        return []

    @staticmethod
    def _set_background(_item, path):
        Gio.Subprocess.new(
            ["omarchy", "theme", "bg", "set", path],
            Gio.SubprocessFlags.NONE,
        )
EOF
nautilus -q
```

Reopen Files. Right-click an image and choose **Set as Omarchy Background**. The stock GNOME item stays in the menu and still does nothing.

Without the extension, set the background from a terminal:

```bash
omarchy theme bg set /path/to/image.jpg
```
records.verify: The background changes at once, and `readlink ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/background` points at the chosen image.

records.title: Fix the Agents widget showing "Codex limits unavailable" with help text `initialize`
records.symptom:
On Omarchy 4.0.1-1 the Agents panel in omarchy-shell shows Codex as **Codex limits unavailable** with the bare help text `initialize`, while local token statistics for Codex still count. `codex login status` says you are logged in. The stored record shows the empty limits:

```
$ jq '{limits, tierLabel, usageStatusText, authHelpText}' ~/.local/state/omarchy/agents/usage/codex.json
{
  "limits": [],
  "tierLabel": "",
  "usageStatusText": "Codex limits unavailable",
  "authHelpText": "initialize"
}
```

Running the collector's own command by hand shows the real error:

```
$ codex -s read-only -a untrusted app-server
error: invalid value 'untrusted' for '--ask-for-approval <APPROVAL_POLICY>'
  [possible values: on-request, never]
```

Reported with codex-cli 0.149.1 and 0.150.1 installed through mise. Seven earlier issues were closed as the same defect.
records.cause: The collector `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex` in 4.0.1-1 starts the Codex app-server with `-a untrusted` (line 531). codex-cli 0.149 removed that approval-policy value and only accepts `on-request` or `never`, so the subprocess exits before the JSON-RPC handshake. Its stderr goes to `DEVNULL`, the `initialize` request never gets a reply, and after 8 seconds `rpc_request` raises `TimeoutError("initialize")`. The except branch stores that exception message as `authHelpText`, which is the word the panel renders. Commit 4cd8a081c (PR #7649, "Fix Codex usage collection on 0.149") changed the value to `on-request` and merged on quattro on 2026-08-25 at 14:07 UTC, about three hours after the v4.0.1 tag, so every 4.0.1-1 install reproduces it. v4.0.2 carries the fix (checked against the v4.0.2 tag and against `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex` on an omarchy 4.0.2-1 install, both read `-a on-request`).
records.fix:
**Omarchy 4.** Update to 4.0.2-1 or later, then refresh the usage records:

```bash
omarchy update
omarchy agent usage-update codex
jq '{tierLabel, usageStatusText, limits}' ~/.local/state/omarchy/agents/usage/codex.json
```

**Stuck on 4.0.1-1 with no update available.** Apply the one-line change from commit 4cd8a081c yourself. The file is package-owned, so the next update overwrites it with the same fix:

```bash
sudo sed -i 's/"-a", "untrusted", "app-server"/"-a", "on-request", "app-server"/' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex
grep -n 'app-server"' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex
omarchy agent usage-update codex
```

Do not try to fix it by wrapping `codex` in `~/.local/bin`. `omarchy-agent-usage-update` calls collectors by absolute path under `$OMARCHY_PATH/bin`, and one reporter found that omarchy-shell's `PATH` puts `~/.local/share/mise/shims` ahead of `~/.local/bin`, so the mise shim wins and the wrapper is ignored by the widget while the same test from a terminal succeeds.
records.verify:
```bash
grep -n 'app-server"' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-agent-usage-codex     # expect -a on-request
omarchy-agent-usage-codex --limits-only | jq '{tierLabel, usageStatusText, limits}'
```

`tierLabel` shows your plan (`plus`, `pro`, `prolite`), `usageStatusText` is empty and `limits` lists the 5h and weekly windows. Reporters confirmed both `-a on-request` and `-a never` return the limits in under a second.

records.title: Fix an NTFS external drive that Files refuses to mount: "volume is dirty and \"force\" flag is not set"
records.symptom:
A USB hard drive formatted NTFS (a WD Elements in the report) shows up in the sidebar of Files (Nautilus) but clicking it gives a generic mount error. The kernel log has the real reason:

```
$ sudo dmesg | tail -n 20
[  118.870318] ntfs3(sda1): It is recommended to use chkdsk.
[  118.934869] ntfs3(sda1): volume is dirty and "force" flag is not set!
```

Reported on Omarchy 4 on an Intel NUC13, one machine.
records.cause: Omarchy mounts NTFS through udisks, which uses the kernel `ntfs3` driver. The volume carries the NTFS dirty flag because Windows did not detach it cleanly (Fast Startup, hibernation, or unplugging without Safely Remove), and `ntfs3` refuses a read/write mount of a dirty volume unless `force` is passed. Files shows only its generic message. The flag is bookkeeping and the files are normally intact. This diagnosis was posted by a helper who reproduced the error text on a test image, and the reporter confirmed the dmesg line and the fix on their drive.
records.fix:
Confirm the cause first. Retry the mount in Files, then read the kernel log and look for the `volume is dirty` line:

```bash
sudo dmesg | tail -n 20
lsblk -f                       # find the NTFS partition if it is not /dev/sda1
```

If anything on the drive is irreplaceable, copy it off first. A read-only mount works while the flag is set:

```bash
udisksctl mount -b /dev/sda1 -o ro
```

Clear the flag. `ntfsfix` is in the `ntfsprogs` package (split out of `ntfs-3g`, extra repo, version 2026.7.7-1 on 2026-09-07), which Omarchy does not install by default.

Omarchy 4:

```bash
omarchy pkg add ntfsprogs
sudo ntfsfix --clear-dirty /dev/sda1
```

Plain Arch:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed ntfsprogs
sudo ntfsfix --clear-dirty /dev/sda1
```

Then mount from Files again, or unplug and replug so udiskie automounts it. If you also use Windows, eject with Safely Remove and turn off Fast Startup (Control Panel, Power Options, "Choose what the power buttons do", untick "Turn on fast startup"), which was offered as the alternative fix but not tested in the thread.
records.verify:
```bash
sudo dmesg | tail -n 5          # no new 'volume is dirty' line after the mount
findmnt -no SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS /dev/sda1
```

A mount made by Files lands under `/run/media/<user>/<label>` with `uid=` and `gid=` set to your ids. The reporter confirmed the drive mounted and all files were readable after `ntfsfix --clear-dirty`.
records.danger: `ntfsfix` is not chkdsk. It clears the dirty flag and repairs a few known inconsistencies, and if it reports errors it cannot fix, stop and let Windows chkdsk run on the drive. Copy irreplaceable data off through the read-only mount before clearing the flag.

records.title: Make LocalSend float again: Omarchy's window rule does not match class `org.localsend.localsend_app`
records.symptom:
LocalSend opens tiled in the active layout instead of as a centered 1100x700 floating window. The older report #7482 adds that clicks do not reach the window's buttons while it is tiled. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.0-1 and 4.0.1-1 with `localsend` 1.18.2-1 from the Arch repos. `hyprctl clients` shows the window's class:

```json
{
  "class": "org.localsend.localsend_app",
  "initialClass": "org.localsend.localsend_app",
  "title": "LocalSend"
}
```
records.cause: `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/apps/localsend.lua` matches the class with `(Share|localsend)` and `localsend`. `o.window` (in `default/hypr/helpers.lua`) puts that string straight into `rules.match.class` and hands it to `hl.window_rule`, and Hyprland 0.56 matches a class against the whole string (RE2 full match), so `(Share|localsend)` cannot match `org.localsend.localsend_app`. An Omarchy collaborator confirmed this in source and reproduced it on a real Hyprland 0.56.2 session: with the stock rules a window with that app id came up `floating=false`, with the corrected pattern it came up floating at 1100x700. Two open pull requests, #7736 and #8878, make the byte-identical change to `default/hypr/apps/localsend.lua`. Neither had merged on 2026-09-07, and the rule on an omarchy 4.0.2-1 install is still the unfixed one.
records.fix:
Until the fix ships, add the corrected rules to your own config. `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` loads Omarchy's defaults first, so a rule placed after the `require` lines wins. Append at the end of the file:

```lua
-- LocalSend's Wayland app id is org.localsend.localsend_app, which the
-- shipped (Share|localsend) rule cannot match. Same rules as omarchy PR #8878.
o.window("^(Share|localsend|org\\.localsend\\.localsend_app)$", { float = true, center = true })
o.window("^(localsend|org\\.localsend\\.localsend_app)$", { size = { 1100, 700 } })
```

Reload and relaunch LocalSend:

```bash
hyprctl reload
```

Remove the two lines once an update ships a `localsend.lua` that names the app id:

```bash
grep -n localsend_app /usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/apps/localsend.lua
```
records.verify:
```bash
hyprctl clients -j | jq '.[] | select(.class == "org.localsend.localsend_app") | {floating, size}'
```

Expect `"floating": true` and `"size": [1100, 700]`. The collaborator's reproduction on Hyprland 0.56.2 gave exactly that with the fixed rules and `floating=false` at the layout's size without them.

records.title: Fix `omarchy update` failing every time at migration 1787515927 (browser policy directories) on Bash 5.3
records.symptom:
`omarchy update` aborts at the same migration on every retry, with nothing between the banner and the failure in the log:

```
Running migration (1787515927)
Stop world-writable Chromium and Firefox policy directories

Something went wrong during the update!

Please review the output above carefully, correct the error, and retry the update.
```

Reported on the edge channel (omarchy `4.0.0.r1872.g7d58bb9-1`) with `bash 5.3.15-1`. Stable 4.0.1 never shipped this migration and stable 4.0.2 ships it with the fix, so this hit edge and dev users between 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-29.
records.cause: Established in #8833. The migration is fine. It calls `omarchy-theme-set-browser`, which runs `omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy`, and that script's `EXIT` trap was `cleanup() { [[ -n $staged ]] && rm -f "$staged"; }`. `staged` is empty on every successful run, so the trap's last command is a false test. Bash 5.3 makes the exit status of the `EXIT` trap the script's exit status, so the script returns 1 after writing every policy file correctly. The migration runs under `bash -euo pipefail`, aborts, and its completion marker is never written, which is why every retry fails identically. A second reporter reproduced it with nothing to harden at all, ruling out any permissions edge case. It is not caused by a missing chromium directory. Fixed in PR #8835, merged as 62eb5182 on 2026-08-29: the trap became an `if` block and the migration now calls `omarchy-theme-set-browser || true` so a cosmetic repaint can no longer block the Firefox hardening after it.
records.fix:
**Omarchy 4.** Update to a build that carries 62eb5182. v4.0.2 does (checked against the tag, the v4.0.2 release notes, and `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy` on an omarchy 4.0.2-1 install):

```bash
omarchy update
```

One reporter on edge did nothing and the next `omarchy update`, after the fix landed, ran the migration through and left `/etc/chromium/policies/managed` and `/opt/zen-browser-bin/distribution` at `0755`.

**Stuck on a build before the fix.** Confirm it is this defect and not a real policy write failure:

```bash
omarchy-theme-set-browser; echo "exit=$?"         # exit=1 with a correct file below is the bug
cat /etc/chromium/policies/managed/color.json
bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; staged=""; cleanup(){ [[ -n $staged ]] && rm -f "$staged"; }; trap cleanup EXIT; exit 0'; echo $?    # prints 1 on bash 5.3
```

The person who diagnosed it posted a marker-file workaround that skips the migration instead of running it, so it is only safe once `/etc/chromium/policies/managed` and any other `policies/managed` directories are already `0755 root:root` and `/usr/lib/firefox/distribution` and `/opt/zen-browser/distribution` are absent or already hardened. Nobody else in the thread confirmed it:

```bash
touch ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/1787515927.sh
omarchy update
```

Do not source the migration into an interactive shell to debug it. One reporter did and saw `command not found: as_root`, which was an artefact of the interactive shell's hooks, not the cause.
records.verify:
```bash
grep -n -A3 '^cleanup' /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy   # if block, not && rm
grep -n 'omarchy-theme-set-browser' /usr/share/omarchy/migrations/1787515927.sh      # ends in || true
omarchy-migrate --pending                                                             # empty
stat -c '%a %U' /etc/chromium/policies/managed /opt/zen-browser/distribution 2>/dev/null
```
records.danger: The marker-file workaround skips the migration that hardens world-writable browser policy directories. Check the directory modes first, and delete the marker later if you want the migration to run for real.

records.title: omarchy update fails at migration 1787515927 on every retry (Bash 5.3 EXIT trap returns 1)
records.symptom:
On the dev channel between 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-29 (reporters on omarchy `4.0.0.r1872.g7d58bb9-1`, bash `5.3.15-1`), `omarchy update` prints `Running migration (1787515927)` / `Stop world-writable Chromium and Firefox policy directories`, then the generic red banner:

```
Something went wrong during the update!
```

`/tmp/omarchy-update.log` shows no error between the migration banner and the failure. Retrying fails at the same point every time, because `omarchy-migrate` only writes the completion marker after the migration script succeeds. Run on its own, the policy script writes the correct file and still reports failure:

```console
$ sudo -n /usr/bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy 060b1e; echo "exit=$?"
exit=1
$ cat /etc/chromium/policies/managed/color.json
{"BrowserThemeColor": "#060b1e", "BrowserColorScheme": "device"}
```
records.cause:
Established in the thread and confirmed by the collaborator who fixed it. `bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy` installed an `EXIT` trap whose handler was `[[ -n $staged ]] && rm -f "$staged"`. `staged` is cleared after each policy file is written, so on every successful run the test is false, the `&&` list short-circuits, and the handler's last status is 1. Bash 5.3 makes the status of the `EXIT` trap's last command the script's exit status, so `exit 0` became exit 1. Bash 5.2 did not. `omarchy-theme-set-browser` propagated that status into a migration running under `bash -euo pipefail`, which aborted the update. Theme switching was not affected because `omarchy-theme-set` does not run under `set -e`. A second reporter reproduced it on a machine where the migration had nothing to harden, which isolated it to the exit status alone. Minimal reproduction without Omarchy:

```console
$ bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; staged=""; cleanup(){ [[ -n $staged ]] && rm -f "$staged"; }; trap cleanup EXIT; exit 0'; echo $?
1
```
records.fix:
Fixed upstream in PR #8835, merged 2026-08-29 as commit `62eb5182`. The migration and the policy script were not in the `v4.0.1` tag (2026-08-25) and first shipped on stable in `v4.0.2` (2026-08-30) already fixed, so only dev-channel installs between those dates hit it. Update to a package that carries the fix:

```bash
omarchy update
```

records.title: Video corruption in Chromium and Electron apps, and a dGPU that never sleeps, on a hybrid laptop whose panel runs on the iGPU
records.symptom:
Omarchy 4.0.1 and 4.0.2 on Intel or AMD laptops with an NVIDIA dGPU that drives no connected display. Chromium, Chrome, Discord and other Electron apps show corrupted or black video, ghosting while scrolling, elements that only paint on mouse hover, or a WebRTC stream that never paints. Launched from a terminal Chromium prints hundreds of:

```
eglCreateImage failed with 0x00003009
Unable to initialize binding from pixmap
OzoneImageBacking::ProduceSkiaGanesh failed to create GL representation
```

`vainfo` reports `VA-API NVDEC driver` instead of the Intel or AMD driver, and the session environment carries the NVIDIA values:

```console
$ systemctl --user show-environment | grep -E 'LIBVA|NVD_BACKEND|__GLX'
LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia
NVD_BACKEND=direct
__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia
```

On battery the dGPU never runtime-suspends while a browser is open: `/sys/bus/pci/devices/<dgpu>/power/runtime_status` stays `active` and `runtime_suspended_time` stays 0. One reporter measured the dGPU at about a third of idle draw on a 99.9 Wh laptop.
records.cause: Established in the thread and confirmed in source by the repository's triage bot. `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/nvidia.lua` (loaded from `default/hypr/envs.lua`, which `default/hypr/omarchy.lua` requires) checks only whether an NVIDIA display-class PCI device exists, via `omarchy-hw-nvidia` and `omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp`, and never whether it drives a display. On Turing or newer (device ID 0x1e00 and up, the GSP branch) it sets `NVD_BACKEND=direct`, `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` and `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia` at config parse. `default/hypr/autostart.lua` then exports the whole environment session-wide on `hyprland.start` with `systemctl --user import-environment` and `dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd --all`, so every app inherits it. On a laptop whose panel is on the iGPU, Chromium decodes video on NVDEC through `libva-nvidia-driver` and presents on the Intel or AMD GPU, and importing those DMA-BUFs into the iGPU fails with `EGL_BAD_MATCH`. Any app touching video decode also opens `/dev/nvidia-uvm`, which blocks runtime suspend. The branch went live in 4.0.1 via commit `33d7363c`, which fixed `o.shell_succeeds()` and un-masked code that had been dead in 4.0.0. All three files above were read on this machine (omarchy 4.0.2-1) and match the thread. Two limits established in the thread: an `hl.env` placed before `require("default.hypr.omarchy")` loses because the default loads after it, and `~/.config/hypr/envs.lua` is never loaded by anything (nothing in `/usr/share/omarchy` requires `hypr.envs`, confirmed here), so an override written there does nothing. Pascal and older cards take a different branch (`NVD_BACKEND=egl`, `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, no `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME`) and one Quadro P520 reporter found the dGPU pinned awake with no CUDA context at all. That machine is not fixed by the override below and the thread had no confirmed fix for it.
records.fix:
No upstream fix has merged as of 2026-09-07. PR #9483 (export the NVIDIA variables only when an NVIDIA card owns a connected display) is open. The override below was verified by the reporter and independently by a second reporter on an HP Arrow Lake plus RTX 5070 laptop, and a Discord-only `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD` restored incoming streams for a third. Put it in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` **after** the line `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`, because the last assignment during parse wins:

```lua
-- ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua, below require("default.hypr.omarchy")
hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "iHD")           -- Intel iGPU
hl.env("__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME", "mesa")
```

The reporter notes `radeonsi` in place of `iHD` for an AMD iGPU. That value was not confirmed by a second reporter in the thread. Then log out and back in. A `hyprctl reload` re-parses the config but the session-wide export only happens on `hyprland.start`, and processes already running keep the old values.

Do not put the override in `~/.config/hypr/envs.lua`, which is not loaded, and do not put it above the `require`. Remove any `--disable-gpu-compositing` line from `~/.config/chromium-flags.conf` or `chrome-flags.conf` afterwards, because both reporters found full GPU compositing works once the driver matches. `--disable-features=VaapiVideoDecoder` does not fix this, because the NVIDIA VA driver still loads.

Apps that should run on the dGPU keep working with PRIME offload scoped to their own launch, for example `__NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1 __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia <game>`.
records.verify:
After a fresh login:

```bash
systemctl --user show-environment | grep -E 'LIBVA|__GLX'   # LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD, __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=mesa
vainfo 2>/dev/null | head -3                                  # Intel iHD driver, not NVDEC
dgpu=$(grep -l 0x10de /sys/bus/pci/devices/*/vendor | head -1 | xargs dirname)
cat "$dgpu/power/runtime_status"                             # suspended, even during YouTube playback
cat "$dgpu/power/runtime_suspended_time"                     # grows over time
```

Chromium should play video with no `eglCreateImage failed with 0x00003009` lines in its terminal output.

records.title: Windows VM launch does nothing after the polkit password (setgid bit on ~/Windows fails the mode check)
records.symptom:
Omarchy 4.0.2-1. Apps menu > Windows, or `omarchy-windows-vm launch`, shows the polkit password dialog, accepts the password, and then nothing happens: no error, no window. Every retry asks for the password again. From a terminal the elevated step exits 1 with no output:

```console
$ stat -c %a ~/Windows
2700
$ pkexec /usr/bin/omarchy-windows-vm __priv up; echo $?
1
```

`omarchy-windows-vm remove` fails the same way with `Windows VM removal stopped before user-side cleanup`, so reinstalling does not help. It hits installs upgraded from 4.0.1 (`~/Windows` at `drwx--S---`) and fresh 4.0.2 installs from the second launch onward. Six reporters confirmed it on Intel and AMD machines, all on kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2, coreutils 9.11 and btrfs.
records.cause: Established by the reporters and confirmed on this machine. `prepare_caller_mounts()` in `/usr/bin/omarchy-windows-vm` (line 583 in omarchy 4.0.2-1) runs `chmod 0700` on the pinned `~/.windows` and `~/Windows` sources and then requires `stat -Lc %a` to return exactly `700`. GNU coreutils `chmod` deliberately preserves a directory's setuid and setgid bits when given a numeric mode of four or fewer digits, so `chmod 0700` leaves `2700` as `2700` and the check returns 1. The same strict `mode == 700` test is in `mounted_leaf_matches()` (line 508), and `assert_mounts_safe` gates `launch`, `install` and `remove`, so none of them can recover. The `dockurr/windows` container sets the shared folder (`~/Windows` on the host) to `2777` when it starts against an **empty** share, which is why the second launch fails on a fresh install. One reporter traced that to the emptiness probe in the image's `/run/samba.sh` and found a non-empty share is left alone. `windows-vm.desktop` has `Terminal=false`, so the failure is invisible. This is coreutils behaviour, not a kernel regression, which the original report first claimed and then retracted.
records.fix:
No upstream fix has merged as of 2026-09-07. PR #9322 (clear the special bits with `chmod u=rwx,go=,a-s` while keeping the strict check) is open. Until it lands, clear the bit in place. Four reporters confirmed this brings the next launch straight up, and it keeps the inode, so the root-owned bind anchor under `/var/lib/omarchy/windows/mounts/users/<uid>/` stays valid:

```bash
chmod g-s ~/Windows ~/.windows
stat -c '%a %n' ~/Windows ~/.windows    # both 700
omarchy-windows-vm launch
```

`chmod 00700 ~/Windows ~/.windows` (five digits) also clears it. `chmod 0700` and `chmod 700` do not.

The bit comes back whenever the container starts against an empty `~/Windows`, so either repeat the `chmod g-s` before each launch, or leave any file in the folder. A dotfile stays hidden from the guest because the generated `smb.conf` keeps Samba's default `hide dot files = yes`:

```bash
touch ~/Windows/.keep
```

Do not move or recreate `~/Windows`. That changes the inode, and the next launch then fails with `protected mount ... no longer matches its home source` until the anchor is unmounted with `pkexec umount /var/lib/omarchy/windows/mounts/users/$(id -u)/shared`.
records.verify:
```bash
stat -c '%a %n' ~/Windows ~/.windows          # 700 and 700, no leading 2
pkexec /usr/bin/omarchy-windows-vm __priv up; echo $?   # 0 and the container comes up
```

records.title: Omawrite's Save File dialog opens larger than the screen at scale 2 (GTK 3 file chooser sizing bug)
records.symptom: Omarchy 4.0.1-2 on a MacBook Air M2 (Asahi), Omawrite 0.5.0-1, GTK 3.24.52, built-in 2560x1664 panel at Hyprland scale 2 (1280x832 logical). Pressing `Ctrl+S` in Omawrite opens a `Save File` window of 1231x950 logical pixels at `(342, -45)`, clipped at the top, right and bottom, so the filename field and the Cancel and Save buttons are hard to reach. `hyprctl clients` shows class `omawrite`, title `Save File`, owned by the Omawrite PID rather than `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk`. Resetting `org.gtk.Settings.FileChooser window-size` to `(-1, -1)` does not help and `GDK_SCALE=1` reproduces the same size. Reported from one machine.
records.cause: Established by the reporter and accepted upstream. Omawrite's Qt Quick `FileDialog` runs under Omarchy's `QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=gtk3`, so it creates a GTK 3 file chooser inside the Omawrite process instead of calling the portal. In GTK 3's `find_good_size_from_style()`, `gtk_style_context_get(..., "font-size", ...)` already returns the computed CSS font size in pixels, but the chooser still multiplied it by `resolution / 72` as if it were points, so the default size came out roughly one third too large. The reporter reproduced it in a standalone `GtkFileChooserDialog` without Omawrite, Qt, Hyprland or Omarchy. GTK's merge request notes the same 1203x902 result was reported upstream with `GDK_SCALE=2`.
records.fix:
Fixed upstream in GTK merge request !10311, merged into the `gtk-3-24` branch on 2026-09-01 as commit `b3034371`. That commit is not in gtk3 3.24.52, which is what Arch ships as of 2026-09-07 (`gtk3 1:3.24.52-1`), so the fix arrives with the next gtk3 release through the normal update:

```bash
omarchy update
pacman -Q gtk3        # needs a version newer than 1:3.24.52-1
```

Until then, the reporter's Hyprland rule constrains only Omawrite's `Save File` window. It was verified on the one machine above and the size is chosen for that display, so adjust it for yours:

```lua
-- ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua, below the require lines
o.window(
  { class = "^omawrite$", title = "^Save File$" },
  { float = true, center = true, size = { 875, 600 } }
)
```

```bash
hyprctl reload
```
records.verify:
Open Omawrite, press `Ctrl+S`, then:

```bash
hyprctl clients | grep -A6 'title: Save File'    # size within the monitor's logical resolution
```

On the reporter's display the rule gave 875x600 at `(203, 130)`, and the patched GTK gave 908x707 with no rule.

records.title: Fix corrupted, stalling or crashing browser video when Omarchy sets LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia on a hybrid laptop whose dGPU drives no output
records.symptom:
On a hybrid laptop (Intel or AMD iGPU driving the panel, NVIDIA dGPU driving nothing) running Omarchy 4.0.1 or 4.0.2, Chromium, Chrome, Edge and Electron apps show video artifacts and glitching, most reliably on a live stream with the chat panel open, hard scroll stalls on video-heavy pages such as reddit.com, Chrome flicker while scrolling, and failed Microsoft Teams meetings. Static pages are smooth and ordinary playback can look fine. Rarely the browser GPU process aborts with `SIGTRAP` and `coredumpctl` records a `chromium` core with `--type=gpu-process`. The session carries `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` and `NVD_BACKEND=direct` even though `/sys/class/drm/` shows every NVIDIA connector `disconnected` and `disabled` while the iGPU's `eDP-1` is `connected`. `vainfo` looks healthy, and installing `intel-media-driver` alone changes nothing. In the browser GPU process the mismatch is visible directly:

```
$ grep -oE '[a-z_]+_drv_video\.so' /proc/$(pgrep -f 'chrome --type=gpu-process')/maps
nvidia_drv_video.so
$ grep -oE 'lib(cuda|nvcuvid)\.so[.0-9]*' /proc/<gpu-process>/maps
libcuda.so.610.57.04
libnvcuvid.so.610.57.04
```

while the same process holds its render node fds on the iGPU (`renderD129`, i915 or amdgpu). Reported on Lenovo Legion 5 15IAX10, Dell RTX 3050 laptop, ThinkPad P1 Gen 6, Razer Blade (AMD Cezanne plus RTX 3080 Mobile), and an Intel Iris Xe plus RTX 3050 Ti Mobile machine, all on 4.0.2-1.
records.cause: Established in the thread by the Omarchy triage collaborator, from source. `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/nvidia.lua` (lines 10 to 14, loaded from `default/hypr/envs.lua:39`) runs `hl.env("NVD_BACKEND", "direct")`, `hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "nvidia")` and `hl.env("__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME", "nvidia")` whenever `bin/omarchy-hw-nvidia` and `bin/omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp` both succeed. Those detectors only check that a PCI device with vendor `0x10de` at class `0x03*` exists and has a device id at or above `0x1e00`. Neither asks whether the NVIDIA GPU renders or scans out anything, and class `0x0302` (3D controller) drives no display by definition. The branch became live in 4.0.1 through commit `33d7363c`, which fixed `o.shell_succeeds()` always returning false inside Hyprland. Under 4.0.0 the whole `if` was dead and these machines were accidentally correct. `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME` overrides libva's DRM-based autodetection, so every VA-API client loads `nvidia_drv_video.so` against the iGPU's render node. Compositing then happens on the iGPU while NVDEC decode runs on the NVIDIA card, and the exported frames cross GPUs. One contributor isolated the rare abort to Chromium's `CHECK_EQ(handle.modifier, object.drm_format_modifier)` in `VaapiWrapper::ExportVASurfaceAsNativePixmapDmaBufUnwrapped`, because `libva-nvidia-driver` returns a different NVIDIA block-linear modifier for the half-height UV plane than for the Y plane. The NVIDIA VA driver is also decode only and exposes no `VAEntrypointEnc*` entrypoints, so the pin removes the iGPU's hardware encode too. Which mechanism breaks Teams was not isolated. Three upstream pull requests (#7851, #9483, #10588) propose different gates and none is merged as of 2026-09-07. Verified on this workstation (omarchy 4.0.2-1): `nvidia.lua` and both detectors read exactly as described.
records.fix:
Omarchy 4 only. Override the variable from your own config, which loads after Omarchy's defaults, so the last `hl.env` assignment wins. Put the line in `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` after `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`. Do not create `~/.config/hypr/envs.lua`: nothing requires that file, so it is never loaded.

Intel iGPU (i915 or xe): install the Intel media driver first, then pin it.

```sh
omarchy update            # fetch the sync databases first on a fresh install
sudo pacman -S intel-media-driver
```

```lua
-- ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua, below require("default.hypr.omarchy")
hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "iHD")
```

AMD iGPU (amdgpu): the Mesa driver is already installed.

```lua
-- ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua, below require("default.hypr.omarchy")
hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "radeonsi")
```

Then log out and back in. `hyprctl reload` re-parses the config and processes Hyprland spawns afterwards do see the new value, but Omarchy's autostart runs `systemctl --user import-environment` at session start and apps launched through systemd user scopes keep the old `nvidia` value until the next login. Fully quit the browser and any Electron app (Discord, Teams) that was started before the change. Each of them keeps the old environment until restarted.

`NVD_BACKEND=direct` is still set by the same branch and is inert once the NVIDIA VA driver is no longer loaded. Leave `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME` alone: the reporters did not test changing it.

On a muxed laptop, or a hybrid laptop whose NVIDIA card actually drives the panel, `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` is the correct setting and this override is wrong. Check which GPU drives the display before applying it:

```sh
for c in /sys/class/drm/card*-*; do printf '%s status=%s enabled=%s\n' "$(basename "$c")" "$(cat "$c/status")" "$(cat "$c/enabled")"; done
readlink -f /sys/class/drm/card*/device | xargs -n1 basename   # PCI address per card
```

If every connector on the NVIDIA card is `disconnected` and `disabled` and only the iGPU's `eDP-1` is `enabled`, the override applies.
records.verify:
After re-login and a browser restart, the GPU process maps the iGPU driver and no longer touches the NVIDIA decode stack:

```sh
GP=$(pgrep -f 'type=gpu-process' | head -n1)
grep -oE '/usr/lib/dri/[a-z0-9_]+_drv_video\.so' /proc/$GP/maps | sort -u
grep -oE 'lib(cuda|nvcuvid)\.so[.0-9]*' /proc/$GP/maps | sort -u
ls -l /proc/$GP/fd | grep -oE 'renderD[0-9]+|nvidia[a-z0-9-]*' | sort | uniq -c
```

Intel: `iHD_drv_video.so` is mapped, the `libcuda`/`libnvcuvid` grep is empty, and the `/dev/nvidia0` and `/dev/nvidia-uvm` fds are gone. AMD: `nvidia_drv_video.so` is absent (the radeonsi driver resolves to `libgallium-*.so`, so grep for its own name never matches) and the count of `/dev/nvidia0` fds is zero. Do not read `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the browser process: Chromium rewrites that region for process titles and it reads back as garbage. The `chrome_crashpad_handler` child inherits the same environment and reads correctly. Reporters confirmed the artifacts, scroll stalls, flicker and Teams failures stopped after the change.

records.title: Stop a plugin file save under ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/ from killing the lock screen with 'Tried to show lockscreen surfaces without active lock'
records.symptom:
The session is locked (idle timeout or `omarchy system lock`). A file inside an enabled local plugin under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` is saved, typically by a background coding agent or an editor still writing after the human walked away. The journal shows `Local plugin changed, reloading: <plugin id>` followed by `lock-stranded: recovering`, and then, seconds or hours later, `omarchy-shell` (Quickshell) aborts:

```
FATAL: Tried to show lockscreen surfaces without active lock
```

Signal `SIGABRT`, process `quickshell -n -p /usr/share/omarchy/shell`, one core in `coredumpctl`. The compositor lock holds, so nothing is exposed. Hyprland shows its crashed-lockscreen fallback, a replacement shell starts within a second or two and the password unlocks it. The abort can be delayed by hours, because the recreated lock service polls a freed object and only trips when the memory is reused, so it can land on a later screen wake with no plugin write anywhere near it. Seen on Omarchy 4.0.1-1 and 4.0.2-1 with Quickshell 0.3.1-1 and Qt 6.11.2, on Intel plus NVIDIA, AMD plus NVIDIA and Apple Silicon (Asahi) machines. One reporter hit it with no lock at all: a plugin being rewritten every 10 to 40 seconds eventually raced the compositor the same way.
records.cause: Established in the thread and confirmed by the merged upstream fix. `reloadPlugins()` in `/usr/share/omarchy/shell/shell.qml` always calls `unloadPluginServices()`, which calls `destroy()` on every service including `omarchy.lock`. The lock plugin's manifest declares `keepLoaded: true`, but until the fix that flag was only honoured for panel Loaders, not services. Destroying the shell's `WlSessionLock` while Hyprland still holds the `ext-session-lock` leaves the compositor locked with no locker client. The recreated lock service tries to recover with `sessionLock.locked = true`, and in Quickshell 0.3.1 `WlSessionLock::realizeLockTarget` calls `qFatal` when `manager->lock()` fails. Quickshell's `QSWaylandSessionLock` destructor also never clears the process-global `manager->active` pointer, so the same shell process can never take a session lock again until it is restarted, and its recovery guard reads a field of the freed object, which is why the abort can come hours later. Verified on this workstation (omarchy 4.0.2-1): `shell.qml:348-354` still destroys every service unconditionally and `keepLoaded` is consulted only at the panel Loader on line 625.
records.fix:
Upstream fix: pull request #9485, "Honor keepLoaded for services during plugin hot-reload", merged to `quattro` on 2026-09-02 as commit `d3d23fdd`. It keeps `keepLoaded` services (lock, idle, polkit, notifications) mounted across a plugin hot-reload. As of 2026-09-07 it is not in any tagged release: `v4.0.2` is the newest tag and does not contain the commit, and the shipped 4.0.2-1 `shell.qml` still has the unconditional teardown. Take it when it ships:

```sh
omarchy update
```

Check whether your installed shell has it:

```sh
grep -n keepLoaded /usr/share/omarchy/shell/shell.qml
```

If the only hits are around the panel Loader (`keepLoaded: m.keepLoaded === true` and the `active:` line), `unloadPluginServices()` is still unpatched.

Until then, prevention is the only fix, because the shell cannot be restarted while locked (`omarchy-restart-shell` refuses when the lock reports secure or requested):

- Do not let anything write into `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` while the session is locked. Stop a background agent or file-watching build that edits a plugin before you lock, or edit the plugin in a scratch directory outside `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` and copy it in when you are at the keyboard.
- If you develop a plugin in place, expect a reload on every save. Each reload while unlocked is harmless, but a reload while locked strands the lock service until the shell dies and restarts.

If the abort has already happened: the compositor lock held, the replacement shell is up, so type your password. Nothing else is needed. If the replacement shell also fails to show a prompt, this is the stranded-lock case: `omarchy-restart-shell` from a TTY (Ctrl+Alt+F3, log in, run it) restarts the shell and re-locks it so you can authenticate.
records.verify:
After the trigger while locked, the journal shows `Local plugin changed, reloading` with no `lock-stranded: recovering` after it, and `coredumpctl list quickshell` shows no new entry:

```sh
journalctl --user -b --no-pager | grep -E 'Local plugin changed|lock-stranded|lockscreen surfaces'
coredumpctl list quickshell
```

The upstream test plan for #9485 checks that after `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins` the lock service's `lastEventAt` is unchanged and its status is not `lock-stranded`.

Covers this issue and already cites it. The thread adds three things: the fix is commit 0965ac2e (PR #6939), cherry-picked as 33d7363c into v4.0.1 and listed in its release notes, so 'fixed in v4.0.1' holds. The record's `omarchy-update` should be `omarchy update`. The record's example sets `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia` unconditionally, which the thread later retracted for hybrid machines (#8215, #8328): on an Intel or AMD iGPU-driven session that value points libva at a driver that rejects the i915 or amdgpu fd, and reporters there want `iHD` or `radeonsi` instead. A pure-NVIDIA desktop reporter also measured that libva 2.24 and libva-nvidia-driver 0.0.17 pick the nvidia driver and the direct backend with none of the three variables set, so their absence did not break VA-API there. Hyprland's `reapZombieChildrenAutomatically()` (SA_NOCLDWAIT) is the pinned mechanism, and `io.popen():close()` status is unreliable for the same reason.

Contradicts the record's cause: the false positive is not Hyprland keeping the unplugged output in its list, it is Hyprland 0.56's FALLBACK output (created the moment the enabled-monitor set empties, and 0.55's HEADLESS-1 before it) reporting disabled=false and matching the name-only check in omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active, which a collaborator reproduced on a 4.0.0 VM. The record's fix still holds and the thread adds two confirmations: plain `hyprctl reload` alone does not help because toggles.lua re-applies the persisted disable, and pressing Super+Ctrl+Delete a second time, blind, takes the on() branch which has no guard and recovers the panel. The helper on this 4.0.2-1 workstation is still the name-only check, PR #8028 was closed unmerged and #7036 and #7207 are open, so the bug is unfixed and the record stays current.

Adds that Omarchy's base set installs gpu-screen-recorder, whose /usr/lib/modprobe.d/gsr-nvidia.conf sets NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1 on every NVIDIA install, while install/hardware/nvidia.sh never enables nvidia-suspend/hibernate/resume on the nvidia-580xx path; the thread is unresolved (one open-module A/B says the services fix it on 610.57.04 Turing, one 580xx Maxwell hybrid still froze with them enabled, and one report says the services make hibernate resume fail on early-KMS installs). The record's `sudo mkinitcpio -P` line is a defect on Omarchy 4 (limine-mkinitcpio), and its claim that open modules never need the services is contradicted by the A/B.

Confirms the fix (`hl.env("LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME", "iHD")`, or `radeonsi` on an AMD iGPU) across more than fifteen Intel+NVIDIA and AMD+NVIDIA laptops on 4.0.1 and 4.0.2, and contradicts the record's cause: the variable is set by /usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/nvidia.lua whenever omarchy-hw-nvidia-gsp matches, was dead on 4.0.0 because o.shell_succeeds always returned false inside Hyprland, and went live with commit 33d7363c in 4.0.1; the compositor and browser GL run on the iGPU while decode is forced onto NVDEC. The record should say the line goes in ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua after require("default.hypr.omarchy") (~/.config/hypr/envs.lua is never loaded, #9902), needs a full logout not hyprctl reload, plus `systemctl --user set-environment LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD` and a full browser quit. PRs #7851 and #9483 are open, none merged.

Same defect as #8215 with the stutter and power-draw angle: dGPU held active in 99% of samples and about 6 W extra while browsing with the stock variables, versus 9% with the iGPU override; one report shows LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME alone lets the dGPU reach D3cold, so __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME need not be overridden. Maxwell/Pascal hybrids take the non-GSP branch and never get LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME, so the fix does not apply there.

Fingerprint unlock hangs 25 to 30 s after resume on an HP EliteBook with a Validity 138a:00ab sensor driven by python-validity-d51-git (AUR) and open-fprintd, not fprintd. Adds the point that restarting the daemon while the lock screen's PAM session is armed produces a ~25 s D-Bus timeout.

Contradicts the record's advice to add a pam_gnome_keyring auth line to /etc/pam.d/sddm: Omarchy 4 strips it on purpose (install/login/sddm.sh) and uses a passwordless Default_keyring whose [keyring] ini stub is valid, and the maintainers' bot showed Chromium's Safe Storage key surviving reboots on a stock install. Same DPMS trigger the record lists as cause (2): EGL error 0x3000 then fatal Wayland error, exit 255, relaunch loop every 1.5 to 2 minutes on a single DP-1 monitor with Intel UHD 630. The reporter stopped it by pinning the monitor's native mode with hl.monitor({ output = "DP-1", mode = "2560x1440@100" }) in ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua, on one machine only, unconfirmed by anyone else, root cause tracked in Quickshell.

Adds the mechanism the maintainers' bot proved in source: Quickshell's realizeLockTarget() builds the LockView and fires the only forcePasswordFocus() before the ext-session-lock request is sent, and nothing refocuses on secure=true, so it misses on every lock for some machines and only after resume for others. Present since 4.0.0, no fix merged, six competing PRs. The workaround is clicking inside the field itself (activeFocusOnPress). The record's hypridle.conf fix is suspect on Omarchy 4, where idle and lock are handled by omarchy-shell and hyprlock is not installed.

Same manual fix (pactl set-card-profile bluez_card.<MAC> headset-head-unit). Adds the cause on WirePlumber 0.5.15 to 0.5.17: selecting the headset input in the Omarchy audio panel triggers the HFP autoswitch, but select-profile.lua treats the EnumProfile change as a new request and find-best-profile.lua puts the card back on a2dp-sink 200 ms later while capture is still linked. Fixed upstream in WirePlumber MR !892, commit f5c3eb35 (2026-09-02), after 0.5.17 was tagged, which is what Arch ships as of 2026-09-07. No Omarchy change needed. PR #9638 remains open.
